source.text: Ἔλεγεν δὲ καὶ πρὸς τοὺς μαθητάς· Ἄνθρωπός τις ἦν πλούσιος ὃς εἶχεν οἰκονόμον, καὶ οὗτος διεβλήθη αὐτῷ ὡς διασκορπίζων τὰ ὑπάρχοντα αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: He was saying now also to the disciples, A man certain there was rich who had a manager, and he was accused to him as wasting the possessions of him.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was also saying to the disciples, "There was a certain rich man who had a manager, and this [manager] was accused to him of wasting his possessions.
en.B: Jesus also told the disciples this: "A rich man had a manager, and word reached him that this man was squandering what he owned.
en.R: Jesus also told {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples this story: "There was once a rich man who had a manager to look after his property. Someone told the rich man that the manager was wasting his money.

es.L: Y decía también a los discípulos: «Era cierto hombre rico que tenía un administrador, y este fue acusado ante él de estar derrochando sus bienes.
es.B: Jesús dijo también a los discípulos: «Un hombre rico tenía un administrador, y le llegaron noticias de que este estaba malgastando lo que él poseía.
es.R: Jesús también les contó esta historia a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos: «Había una vez un hombre rico que tenía un administrador que se ocupaba de sus propiedades. Alguien le contó al hombre rico que el administrador estaba malgastando su dinero.

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} disait aussi aux disciples : « Il y avait un homme riche qui avait un intendant, et celui-ci lui a été dénoncé comme dissipant ses biens.
fr.B: Jésus dit aussi aux disciples : « Un homme riche avait un intendant, et on lui a rapporté que cet homme gaspillait ses biens.
fr.R: Jésus a aussi raconté cette histoire à {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples : « Il y avait un homme riche qui avait un intendant pour s’occuper de ses biens. Quelqu’un a dit à l’homme riche que l’intendant gaspillait son argent.

sw.L: Naye alikuwa akisema pia kwa wanafunzi, "Mtu fulani alikuwa tajiri, ambaye alikuwa na msimamizi; na huyu akashtakiwa mbele yake kuwa anafuja mali zake.
sw.B: Yesu aliwaambia pia wanafunzi jambo hili: "Mtu mmoja tajiri alikuwa na msimamizi, naye akapata habari kwamba msimamizi huyo alikuwa akifuja mali zake.
sw.R: Yesu aliwasimulia pia wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} hadithi hii: "Kulikuwa na mtu tajiri aliyekuwa na msimamizi wa kutunza mali zake. Mtu fulani akamwambia yule tajiri kwamba msimamizi huyo alikuwa akitumia vibaya fedha zake.

decisions.choice: manager: a steward who ran a rich man's estate and business for him
alternatives: a household slave with no authority
decisions.reason: A manager could make contracts, lend goods and collect debts in his master's name (12:42). Here he has charge of what the rich man owns and of the accounts of those who owe him.

decisions.choice: was accused: was reported, charged with wrongdoing
decisions.reason: The verb is often used of a hostile report, sometimes a false one. The manager does not deny it, and 16:8 calls him dishonest.

decisions.choice: wasting: scattering, letting it slip away
decisions.reason: The same verb is used of the younger son in 15:13. The charge is careless or wasteful handling of his master's goods.

decisions.choice: also to the disciples: the same audience as chapter 15, with the disciples now addressed
decisions.reason: "Also" links this parable with the three before it. The Pharisees are still listening (16:14).

decisions.choice: to look after his property; Someone told the rich man
alternatives: a manager; was accused to him
decisions.reason: Readable says what a manager did and turns the passive into a plain sentence.

decisions.choice: the quotation opens here and runs on to 16:13; the speakers' words are in single quotation marks
alternatives: a quotation for the parable only
decisions.reason: The parable and the sayings after it (16:8-13) are one speech of Jesus.

decisions.choice: administrador
decisions.reason: The steward ran his master's estate and business for him (meaning decision m1). "Administrador" says what he did; "mayordomo" now suggests the head servant of a house. The same through 16:8.

decisions.choice: « opens here and closes at the end of 16:13; the rich man's and the manager's words are in “ ”
decisions.reason: Jesus' story runs on to 16:13, as in the English. Spanish marks the speech inside it with “ ”, the second level of quotation marks.

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B) and the passé composé (R); the two parables (16:1-8, 16:19-31) are Jesus' speech, in the passé composé at every level, with the historic presents of 16:7, 16:23 and 16:29 kept at Literal
alternatives: the parables in the passé simple at Literal and Balanced
decisions.reason: As in Luke 15: the passé simple is the normal tense of written narrative, and Readable uses the passé composé, as French is spoken and read in school today. Jesus' stories are speech, so they keep the tenses of speech at every level, as the style guide asks. This holds for the whole chapter.

decisions.choice: un intendant
decisions.reason: As in Luke 12:42: "intendant" is the French word for the man who runs an estate for its owner (m1); "économe" now suggests a school bursar or a thrifty person, and "gérant" a shop manager. Literal says "dissipant", the verb of 15:13, as the Greek repeats it (m3).

decisions.choice: msimamizi
decisions.reason: The steward ran his master's estate and business for him (meaning decision m1). "Msimamizi" (manager, overseer) says that; "wakili" today means mainly a lawyer. The same through 16:8.

source.text: καὶ φωνήσας αὐτὸν εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Τί τοῦτο ἀκούω περὶ σοῦ;

records.literal_gloss: And having called him he said to him, What [is] this I hear concerning you?

en.L: And calling him, he said to him, 'What is this I hear about you?
en.B: So he sent for him and said, 'What is this that I keep hearing about you?
en.R: So he called the manager in and said to him, 'I have heard things about you. What is going on?

es.L: Y llamándolo, le dijo: “¿Qué es esto que oigo de ti?
es.B: Entonces lo mandó llamar y le dijo: “¿Qué es esto que no dejo de oír acerca de ti?
es.R: Entonces llamó al administrador y le dijo: “He oído cosas de ti. ¿Qué está pasando?

fr.L: Et l’ayant appelé, il lui a dit : “Qu’est-ce que j’entends dire de toi ?
fr.B: Il l’a donc fait venir et lui a dit : “Qu’est-ce que j’entends sans cesse raconter à ton sujet ?
fr.R: Alors il a fait venir l’intendant et lui a dit : “J’ai entendu des choses sur toi. Qu’est-ce qui se passe ?

sw.L: Naye akiisha kumwita, akamwambia, 'Ni nini hiki ninachokisikia kuhusu wewe?
sw.B: Basi alimwita, akamwambia, 'Ni mambo gani haya ninayozidi kuyasikia kukuhusu?
sw.R: Basi alimwita msimamizi, akamwambia, 'Nimesikia mambo fulani kukuhusu. Kuna nini?

decisions.choice: What is this I hear: a demand for an answer, not a request for news
decisions.reason: The question already assumes the report is true. The next sentence dismisses him.

decisions.choice: a statement, then the question
decisions.reason: Readable breaks the question into two short sentences.

decisions.choice: his words open here and run on to 16:2b
decisions.reason: The master's words are one speech.

decisions.choice: Jesus' words in « », the words of the people in his stories in “ ”
alternatives: the English pattern of double and single marks
decisions.reason: French typography nests « » and then “ ”, as in Luke 15. The master's words open here and run on to 16:2b.

source.text: ἀπόδος τὸν λόγον τῆς οἰκονομίας σου, οὐ γὰρ δύνῃ ἔτι οἰκονομεῖν.

records.literal_gloss: Give the account of the stewardship of you, not for you are able any longer to manage.

en.L: Give the account of your management, for you can no longer manage.'
en.B: Hand in a report on how you have managed my affairs, because you cannot be my manager any longer.'
en.R: Give me a full report of the work you have done for me. You cannot be my manager anymore.'

es.L: Da la cuenta de tu administración, porque ya no puedes administrar”.
es.B: Entrégame un informe de cómo has administrado mis asuntos, porque ya no puedes seguir siendo mi administrador”.
es.R: Dame un informe completo del trabajo que has hecho para mí. Ya no puedes ser mi administrador”.

fr.L: Rends le compte de ta gestion, car tu ne peux plus gérer.”
fr.B: Remets-moi le compte rendu de ta gestion, car tu ne peux plus être mon intendant.”
fr.R: Donne-moi un rapport complet sur tout le travail que tu as fait pour moi. Tu ne peux plus être mon intendant.”

sw.L: Toa hesabu ya usimamizi wako, kwa maana huwezi tena kusimamia.'
sw.B: Lete taarifa ya jinsi ulivyosimamia mambo yangu, kwa sababu huwezi kuwa msimamizi wangu tena.'
sw.R: Niletee taarifa kamili ya kazi uliyonifanyia. Huwezi kuwa msimamizi wangu tena.'

decisions.choice: give the account of your management: hand over the accounts, so that the estate can pass to someone else
decisions.reason: "Account" here is a business record. He is to give up the books before he goes.

decisions.choice: you can no longer manage: you are dismissed
alternatives: you are not able to do the work
decisions.reason: The master has decided. The manager has only a short time before he must leave.

source.text: εἶπεν δὲ ἐν ἑαυτῷ ὁ οἰκονόμος· Τί ποιήσω ὅτι ὁ κύριός μου ἀφαιρεῖται τὴν οἰκονομίαν ἀπ’ ἐμοῦ;

records.literal_gloss: Said then within himself the manager, What shall I do, for the master of me is taking away the management from me?

en.L: And the manager said within himself, 'What shall I do, since my master is taking the management away from me?
en.B: The manager thought it over: 'My master is taking my position from me. What am I to do?
en.R: The manager thought to himself, 'What can I do? My master is going to take my job away from me.

es.L: Y dijo dentro de sí el administrador: “¿Qué haré, ya que mi señor me quita la administración?
es.B: El administrador se puso a pensar: “Mi señor me quita el puesto. ¿Qué voy a hacer?
es.R: El administrador pensó: “¿Qué puedo hacer? Mi señor me va a quitar el trabajo.

fr.L: Et l’intendant a dit en lui-même : “Que ferai-je, puisque mon maître me retire la gestion ?
fr.B: L’intendant a réfléchi : “Mon maître me retire mon poste. Que vais-je faire ?
fr.R: L’intendant a pensé : “Qu’est-ce que je peux faire ? Mon maître va me prendre mon travail.

sw.L: Na yule msimamizi akasema ndani yake, 'Nitafanya nini, kwa kuwa bwana wangu ananinyang'anya usimamizi?
sw.B: Msimamizi alitafakari, 'Bwana wangu ananinyang'anya cheo changu. Nifanye nini sasa?
sw.R: Msimamizi aliwaza moyoni, 'Nifanye nini? Bwana wangu ataninyang'anya kazi yangu.

decisions.choice: said within himself: thought to himself
decisions.reason: Luke often lets readers hear a person's thoughts this way (12:17; 15:17-19).

decisions.choice: master: the rich man in the parable
decisions.reason: The word can mean "lord" or "master". In the parable it is the owner of the estate, as in 12:42-46.

decisions.choice: the reason first, then the question
decisions.reason: Balanced puts the cause first; the meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: his thoughts open here and run on to 16:4
decisions.reason: The manager's thoughts are one speech to himself.

decisions.choice: mi señor, lowercase, with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: The master is the rich man of the parable (meaning decision m2), a figure in a story, so he is "señor" with a small letter and his pronouns take no setting, as in Matthew's parables.

decisions.choice: bwana wangu, lowercase, with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: The master is the rich man of the parable (meaning decision m2), a figure in a story, so he is "bwana" with a small letter and his pronouns take no setting, as in Matthew's parables.

source.text: σκάπτειν οὐκ ἰσχύω, ἐπαιτεῖν αἰσχύνομαι·

records.literal_gloss: To dig not I am able, to beg I am ashamed.

en.L: I am not strong enough to dig; I am ashamed to beg.
en.B: Digging is too hard for me, and I would be ashamed to beg.
en.R: I am not strong enough to work digging in the fields. And I would be too ashamed to beg for money.

es.L: Cavar, no tengo fuerzas; mendigar, me da vergüenza.
es.B: Cavar es demasiado duro para mí, y me daría vergüenza pedir limosna.
es.R: No tengo fuerzas para trabajar cavando en el campo. Y me daría mucha vergüenza pedirle dinero a la gente.

fr.L: Bêcher, je n’en ai pas la force ; mendier, j’en ai honte.
fr.B: Travailler la terre, c’est trop dur pour moi, et j’aurais honte de mendier.
fr.R: Je ne suis pas assez fort pour travailler la terre dans les champs. Et j’aurais trop honte de demander de l’argent aux gens.

sw.L: Kuchimba sina nguvu; kuombaomba naona aibu.
sw.B: Kazi ya kuchimba ni ngumu mno kwangu, na ningeona aibu kuombaomba.
sw.R: Sina nguvu za kufanya kazi ya kuchimba mashambani. Tena ningeona aibu sana kuwaomba watu pesa.

decisions.choice: to dig; to beg: the work of the poorest laborers, and the life of those who could not work
decisions.reason: Digging was hard work for day laborers. A man who had lived as a manager would not have the strength for it, and begging would shame him.

decisions.choice: I am not able: I am not strong enough
decisions.reason: The verb means to have strength.

decisions.choice: in the fields; for money
decisions.reason: Readable fills out the two pictures.

decisions.choice: kuchimba (dig)
decisions.reason: The verb is to dig, the heavy work of the poorest laborers (meaning decision m1). "Kuchimba" says that; "kulima" (to hoe, to farm) is a familiar wording but turns it into farming one's own land.

source.text: ἔγνων τί ποιήσω, ἵνα ὅταν μετασταθῶ ἐκ τῆς οἰκονομίας δέξωνταί με εἰς τοὺς οἴκους ἑαυτῶν.

records.literal_gloss: I know what I will do, so that when I shall have been removed from the management, they might receive me into the homes of them.

en.L: I know what I will do, so that when I am removed from the management, they may receive me into their homes.'
en.B: Now I know what I will do, so that when I am put out of my job, people will open their homes to me.'
en.R: I know what I will do! Then, when I lose my job, people will be my friends and welcome me into their homes.'

es.L: Ya sé qué haré, para que, cuando sea removido de la administración, me reciban en sus casas”.
es.B: Ya sé lo que haré, para que, cuando me quiten el puesto, haya gente que me abra las puertas de su casa”.
es.R: ¡Ya sé lo que voy a hacer! Así, cuando me quede sin trabajo, la gente será amiga mía y me recibirá en sus casas”.

fr.L: Je sais ce que je ferai, afin que, quand j’aurai été écarté de la gestion, ils me reçoivent dans leurs maisons.”
fr.B: Voilà, je sais ce que je vais faire pour que, lorsque j’aurai perdu ma place, des gens m’ouvrent leur maison.”
fr.R: Je sais ce que je vais faire ! Comme ça, quand j’aurai perdu mon travail, des gens seront mes amis et m’accueilleront chez eux.”

sw.L: Nimejua nitakalofanya, ili nitakapoondolewa kutoka usimamizi, wanipokee katika nyumba zao.'
sw.B: Sasa najua nitakachofanya, ili nikifukuzwa kazi, watu wanifungulie milango ya nyumba zao.'
sw.R: Nimepata wazo! Nitakapopoteza kazi yangu, watu watakuwa rafiki zangu na kunikaribisha nyumbani kwao.'

decisions.choice: I know: a sudden idea, "I have it"
decisions.reason: The verb form describes a moment of decision: the plan comes to him all at once.

decisions.choice: they: the people who owe his master, as 16:5 shows
decisions.reason: The Greek does not say who will receive him. The next verses show whom he means.

decisions.choice: receive me into their homes: give him a place and support, as people do for one who has done them a favor
decisions.reason: In that world a favor put the one who received it under obligation to repay. The manager makes friends who will owe him.

decisions.choice: people
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable avoid a "they" with nothing before it to refer to.

source.text: καὶ προσκαλεσάμενος ἕνα ἕκαστον τῶν χρεοφειλετῶν τοῦ κυρίου ἑαυτοῦ ἔλεγεν τῷ πρώτῳ· Πόσον ὀφείλεις τῷ κυρίῳ μου;

records.literal_gloss: And having called to [him] one each of the debtors of the master of himself he was saying to the first, How much owe you to the master of me?

en.L: And calling to [him] each one of his own master's debtors, he said to the first, 'How much do you owe my master?'
en.B: He sent for his master's debtors one by one. To the first he said, 'How much do you owe my master?'
en.R: So he called in all the people who owed his master something, one at a time. He asked the first one, 'How much do you owe my master?'

es.L: Y llamando a cada uno de los deudores de su propio señor, decía al primero: “¿Cuánto debes a mi señor?”.
es.B: Mandó llamar uno por uno a los deudores de su señor. Al primero le dijo: “¿Cuánto le debes a mi señor?”.
es.R: Entonces llamó, uno por uno, a todos los que le debían algo a su señor. Al primero le preguntó: “¿Cuánto le debes a mi señor?”.

fr.L: Et, ayant fait venir un à un chacun des débiteurs de son maître, il a dit au premier : “Combien dois-tu à mon maître ?”
fr.B: Il a fait venir un par un les débiteurs de son maître. Il a demandé au premier : “Combien dois-tu à mon maître ?”
fr.R: Alors il a fait venir, l’un après l’autre, tous les gens qui devaient quelque chose à son maître. Il a demandé au premier : “Combien est-ce que tu dois à mon maître ?”

sw.L: Na baada ya kuwaita kwake mmoja mmoja wadeni wa bwana wake mwenyewe, alikuwa akimwambia wa kwanza, 'Unadaiwa kiasi gani na bwana wangu?'
sw.B: Basi aliwaita wadeni wa bwana wake mmoja mmoja. Akamwuliza wa kwanza, 'Bwana wangu anakudai kiasi gani?'
sw.R: Basi aliwaita, mmoja baada ya mwingine, watu wote waliokuwa na deni kwa bwana wake. Akamwuliza wa kwanza, 'Bwana wangu anakudai kiasi gani?'

decisions.choice: debtors: tenants or traders who owed the estate goods, often a share of the harvest
alternatives: people who had borrowed money at interest
decisions.reason: Debts were often counted in produce: oil and wheat in the next verses. Tenant farmers paid rent in kind, and merchants might owe for goods received.

decisions.choice: one each: one at a time
decisions.reason: He deals with each debtor alone, so that each owes the favor to him.

source.text: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· Ἑκατὸν βάτους ἐλαίου· ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Δέξαι σου τὰ γράμματα καὶ καθίσας ταχέως γράψον πεντήκοντα.

records.literal_gloss: He and said, A hundred baths of oil. He and said to him, Take your the bill and having sat down quickly write fifty.

en.L: And he said, 'A hundred baths of oil.' And he said to him, 'Take your bill, and sit down quickly [and] write fifty.'
en.B: '{{units:About 600 gallons|A hundred baths}} of olive oil,' he answered. The manager told him, 'Here is your bill. Sit down quickly and write {{units:300 gallons|fifty}}.'
en.R: The man answered, '{{units:About 600 gallons|A hundred baths}} of olive oil.' The manager said to him, 'Take your bill. Sit down quickly and change it to {{units:300 gallons|fifty baths}}.'

es.L: Y él dijo: “Cien batos de aceite”. Y él le dijo: “Toma tu pagaré, y sentándote pronto, escribe cincuenta”.
es.B: “{{units:Unos 2200 litros|Cien batos}} de aceite de oliva”, contestó él. El administrador le dijo: “Aquí tienes tu pagaré. Siéntate enseguida y escribe {{units:1100 litros|cincuenta}}”.
es.R: El hombre respondió: “{{units:Unos 2200 litros|Cien batos}} de aceite de oliva”. El administrador le dijo: “Toma el papel de tu deuda. Siéntate rápido y cámbialo a {{units:1100 litros|cincuenta batos}}”.

fr.L: Et celui-ci a dit : “Cent baths d’huile.” Et il lui a dit : “Prends ton billet, assieds-toi vite [et] écris cinquante.”
fr.B: “{{units:Environ 2 200 litres|Cent baths}} d’huile d’olive”, a-t-il répondu. L’intendant lui a dit : “Voici ta reconnaissance de dette. Assieds-toi vite et écris {{units:1 100 litres|cinquante}}.”
fr.R: L’homme a répondu : “{{units:Environ 2 200 litres|Cent baths}} d’huile d’olive.” L’intendant lui a dit : “Prends ton papier. Assieds-toi vite et change le chiffre : écris {{units:1 100 litres|cinquante baths}}.”

sw.L: Naye akasema, 'Bathi mia moja za mafuta.' Naye akamwambia, 'Pokea hati yako, na ukiketi upesi, andika hamsini.'
sw.B: Alijibu, '{{units:Karibu lita 2,200|Bathi mia moja}} za mafuta ya zeituni.' Msimamizi akamwambia, 'Hii hapa hati yako. Keti haraka uandike {{units:lita 1,100|hamsini}}.'
sw.R: Mtu huyo alijibu, '{{units:Karibu lita 2,200|Bathi mia moja}} za mafuta ya zeituni.' Msimamizi akamwambia, 'Chukua hati ya deni lako. Keti haraka uibadilishe iwe {{units:lita 1,100|bathi hamsini}}.'

decisions.choice: a hundred baths of oil: a large debt of olive oil
alternatives: a small amount for one household
decisions.reason: The bath was a Hebrew measure for liquids (1 Kings 7:26; Ezekiel 45:10-14). Its size is not known exactly: a jar marked as a bath found in Judah held about 22 liters (about 6 gallons), while Josephus suggests a larger measure. A hundred baths is roughly 2,200 liters or more, the yield of a large olive grove.

decisions.choice: bill: the written agreement or note of the debt
decisions.reason: The word means writings, here the document that recorded what the debtor owed. The debtor writes the new figure in his own hand.

decisions.choice: fifty: he cuts the debt in half
decisions.reason: The manager has the debtor change the amount on the bill. Whether he was removing his own commission, the interest, or simply his master's goods, the text does not say; 16:8 calls him dishonest.

decisions.choice: {{units:About 600 gallons|A hundred baths}}; {{units:300 gallons|fifty}} (B), {{units:300 gallons|fifty baths}} (R)
alternatives: a hundred baths at every level
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give a modern measure by default, with the original measure as the alternative. Literal keeps the bath. The figure follows the smaller, better-attested size of the bath; a larger estimate would give about 800 or 900 gallons.

decisions.choice: olive oil
decisions.reason: The oil of that land was olive oil.

decisions.choice: change it to
decisions.reason: Readable says what writing the new figure meant.

decisions.choice: {{units:Unos 2200 litros|Cien batos}}; {{units:1100 litros|cincuenta}} (B), {{units:1100 litros|cincuenta batos}} (R); batos (L)
decisions.reason: The English converts to US gallons; Spanish uses metric measures by default, reckoning the bath at about 22 litres (meaning decision m1, uncertain). Literal keeps the Hebrew measure, and the setting gives it back at Balanced and Readable.

decisions.choice: pagaré (L, B); el papel de tu deuda (R)
decisions.reason: The bill is the written note of the debt (meaning decision m2). "Pagaré" is a signed promise to pay; "recibo" would be proof of a payment already made. Readable says it plainly.

decisions.choice: {{units:Environ 2 200 litres|Cent baths}}; {{units:1 100 litres|cinquante}} (B), {{units:1 100 litres|cinquante baths}} (R)
decisions.reason: French gives the metric measure by default, with the original measure as the alternative, where the English gives US gallons. The figure takes the same bath as the English (about 22 litres); Literal keeps "baths".

decisions.choice: {{units:Karibu lita 2,200|Bathi mia moja}}; {{units:lita 1,100|hamsini}} (B), {{units:lita 1,100|bathi hamsini}} (R); bathi (L)
decisions.reason: The English converts to US gallons; Swahili uses metric measures by default, reckoning the bath at about 22 litres (meaning decision m1, uncertain). "Bathi" is the Hebrew measure; Literal keeps it, and the setting gives it back at Balanced and Readable.

source.text: ἔπειτα ἑτέρῳ εἶπεν· Σὺ δὲ πόσον ὀφείλεις;

records.literal_gloss: Then to another he said, You now how much owe?

en.L: Then to another he said, 'And you, how much do you owe?'
en.B: Then he said to another, 'And what do you owe?'
en.R: Then he asked another man, 'How much do you owe?'

es.L: Después dijo a otro: “Y tú, ¿cuánto debes?”.
es.B: Luego le dijo a otro: “¿Y tú cuánto debes?”.
es.R: Después le preguntó a otro hombre: “¿Cuánto debes?”.

fr.L: Ensuite il a dit à un autre : “Et toi, combien dois-tu ?”
fr.B: Puis il a dit à un autre : “Et toi, que dois-tu ?”
fr.R: Puis il a demandé à un autre homme : “Combien est-ce que tu dois ?”

sw.L: Kisha akamwambia mwingine, 'Na wewe, unadaiwa kiasi gani?'
sw.B: Kisha akamwambia mwingine, 'Na wewe je, unadaiwa kiasi gani?'
sw.R: Kisha akamwuliza mtu mwingine, 'Unadaiwa kiasi gani?'

decisions.choice: another: a second debtor, one example of the many
decisions.reason: Two examples show what he did with each debtor (16:5).

source.text: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· Ἑκατὸν κόρους σίτου· λέγει αὐτῷ· Δέξαι σου τὰ γράμματα καὶ γράψον ὀγδοήκοντα.

records.literal_gloss: He and said, A hundred cors of wheat. He says to him, Take your the bill and write eighty.

en.L: And he said, 'A hundred cors of wheat.' He says to him, 'Take your bill and write eighty.'
en.B: '{{units:About 600 bushels|A hundred cors}} of wheat,' he replied. The manager told him, 'Take your bill and write {{units:about 500|eighty}}.'
en.R: '{{units:About 600 bushels|A hundred cors}} of wheat,' the man said. The manager told him, 'Take your bill and change it to {{units:about 500 bushels|eighty cors}}.'

es.L: Y él dijo: “Cien coros de trigo”. Le dice: “Toma tu pagaré y escribe ochenta”.
es.B: “{{units:Unos 22.000 litros|Cien coros}} de trigo”, respondió. El administrador le dijo: “Toma tu pagaré y escribe {{units:unos 17.600 litros|ochenta}}”.
es.R: “{{units:Unos 22.000 litros|Cien coros}} de trigo”, dijo el hombre. El administrador le dijo: “Toma el papel de tu deuda y cámbialo a {{units:unos 17.600 litros|ochenta coros}}”.

fr.L: Et celui-ci a dit : “Cent cors de blé.” Il lui dit : “Prends ton billet et écris quatre-vingts.”
fr.B: “{{units:Environ 22 000 litres|Cent cors}} de blé”, a-t-il répondu. L’intendant lui a dit : “Prends ta reconnaissance de dette et écris {{units:17 600|quatre-vingts}}.”
fr.R: “{{units:Environ 22 000 litres|Cent cors}} de blé”, a dit l’homme. L’intendant lui a dit : “Prends ton papier et change le chiffre : écris {{units:17 600 litres|quatre-vingts cors}}.”

sw.L: Naye akasema, 'Kori mia moja za ngano.' Anamwambia, 'Pokea hati yako, uandike themanini.'
sw.B: Alijibu, '{{units:Karibu lita 22,000|Kori mia moja}} za ngano.' Msimamizi akamwambia, 'Chukua hati yako uandike {{units:lita 17,600 hivi|themanini}}.'
sw.R: Mtu huyo alisema, '{{units:Karibu lita 22,000|Kori mia moja}} za ngano.' Msimamizi akamwambia, 'Chukua hati ya deni lako, uibadilishe iwe {{units:karibu lita 17,600|kori themanini}}.'

decisions.choice: a hundred cors of wheat: a very large debt of grain
decisions.reason: The cor was the largest Hebrew dry measure, equal to ten baths (Ezekiel 45:14). On the measure of about 22 liters for a bath, a hundred cors is about 22,000 liters, the harvest of a large farm. Like the oil in 16:6, the size is uncertain.

decisions.choice: eighty: he cuts the debt by a fifth
decisions.reason: Twenty cors of wheat was a large sum, perhaps close in value to the fifty baths of oil.

decisions.choice: {{units:About 600 bushels|A hundred cors}}; {{units:about 500|eighty}} (B), {{units:about 500 bushels|eighty cors}} (R)
alternatives: a hundred cors at every level
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give a modern measure by default, with the original measure as the alternative, on the same size of bath as 16:6. Literal keeps the cor.

decisions.choice: The manager
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the speaker.

decisions.choice: change it to
decisions.reason: As in 16:6.

decisions.choice: {{units:Unos 22.000 litros|Cien coros}}; {{units:unos 17.600 litros|ochenta}} (B), {{units:unos 17.600 litros|ochenta coros}} (R); coros (L)
decisions.reason: As with the oil in 16:6: metric by default, reckoning the cor at about 220 litres (meaning decision m1, uncertain), where the English has bushels. Literal keeps the Hebrew measure. Literal also keeps the present "le dice", as the English Literal "he says".

decisions.choice: {{units:Environ 22 000 litres|Cent cors}}; {{units:17 600|quatre-vingts}} (B), {{units:17 600 litres|quatre-vingts cors}} (R)
decisions.reason: As in 16:6: metric by default, the original measure as the alternative, where the English gives bushels; a cor held ten baths, about 220 litres. Literal keeps "cors" and the present "il lui dit".

decisions.choice: {{units:Karibu lita 22,000|Kori mia moja}}; {{units:lita 17,600 hivi|themanini}} (B), {{units:karibu lita 17,600|kori themanini}} (R); kori (L)
decisions.reason: As with the oil in 16:6: metric by default, reckoning the cor at about 220 litres (meaning decision m1, uncertain), where the English has bushels. Literal keeps the Hebrew measure and the present "anamwambia", as the English Literal "he says".

source.text: καὶ ἐπῄνεσεν ὁ κύριος τὸν οἰκονόμον τῆς ἀδικίας ὅτι φρονίμως ἐποίησεν· ὅτι οἱ υἱοὶ τοῦ αἰῶνος τούτου φρονιμώτεροι ὑπὲρ τοὺς υἱοὺς τοῦ φωτὸς εἰς τὴν γενεὰν τὴν ἑαυτῶν εἰσιν.

records.literal_gloss: And praised the master the manager of unrighteousness because shrewdly he had acted; for the sons of the age this more shrewd than the sons of the light toward the generation of themselves are.

en.L: And the master praised the manager of unrighteousness because he had acted shrewdly; for the {{gender:children|sons}} of this age are more shrewd toward their own generation than the {{gender:children|sons}} of the light.
en.B: So the master gave the dishonest manager credit for acting so shrewdly. For the people of this age deal more shrewdly with others of their own kind than the people of the light do.
en.R: When the master heard about it, he praised the dishonest manager for being so clever. People who belong to this world are wiser in dealing with each other than people who belong to the light.

es.L: Y el señor alabó al administrador de injusticia porque había obrado sagazmente; pues los hijos de esta era son más sagaces para con su propia generación que los hijos de la luz.
es.B: Y el señor elogió al administrador deshonesto por haber actuado con tanta sagacidad. Porque la gente de esta era es más sagaz en el trato con los de su misma clase que la gente de la luz.
es.R: Cuando el señor se enteró, felicitó al administrador deshonesto por haber sido tan listo. La gente que pertenece a este mundo es más lista para tratar con los suyos que la gente que pertenece a la luz.

fr.L: Et le maître a loué l’intendant d’injustice parce qu’il avait agi avec habileté ; car les {{gender:enfants|fils}} de ce siècle sont plus habiles envers leur propre génération que les {{gender:enfants|fils}} de la lumière.
fr.B: Et le maître a félicité l’intendant malhonnête d’avoir agi avec tant d’habileté. Car les gens de ce monde sont plus habiles dans leurs rapports avec leurs semblables que les gens de la lumière.
fr.R: Quand le maître l’a appris, il a félicité l’intendant malhonnête parce qu’il avait été très malin. Les gens qui appartiennent à ce monde savent mieux s’y prendre entre eux que les gens qui appartiennent à la lumière.

sw.L: Na bwana akamsifu yule msimamizi wa udhalimu kwa sababu alitenda kwa werevu; kwa kuwa wana wa zama hizi ni werevu zaidi kuelekea kizazi chao wenyewe kuliko wana wa nuru.
sw.B: Basi bwana wake alimsifu msimamizi huyo mdanganyifu kwa kutenda kwa werevu namna hiyo. Kwa maana watu wa zama hizi ni werevu zaidi katika kushughulika na watu wa aina yao kuliko watu wa nuru.
sw.R: Bwana wake aliposikia habari hiyo, alimsifu yule msimamizi mdanganyifu kwa werevu wake. Watu walio wa ulimwengu huu wana akili zaidi katika kushughulikiana wao kwa wao kuliko watu walio wa nuru.

decisions.choice: the master: the rich man in the parable
decisions.reason: The word is the one used for the master in 16:3 and 16:5, so it most likely means the same man. Some take it as Luke's name for Jesus (as in 18:6), which would make Jesus the one who praises. The verse goes on to Jesus' own comment.

decisions.choice: manager of unrighteousness: the dishonest manager
alternatives: a manager of a wicked master
decisions.reason: "Of unrighteousness" describes the manager, a Hebrew way of saying "unrighteous" (compare 18:6, "judge of unrighteousness").

decisions.choice: shrewdly: with practical wisdom, thinking ahead
decisions.reason: The master praises his foresight, not his dishonesty. The same word describes the wise manager in 12:42.

decisions.choice: the sons of this age; the sons of the light: people who belong to this present world, and people who belong to God
decisions.reason: "Son of" was a Hebrew way of saying that a person belonged to or shared the nature of something (10:6; John 12:36; 1 Thessalonians 5:5). Jewish writings of the time also speak of the sons of light.

decisions.choice: toward their own generation: in dealing with people of their own kind
decisions.reason: People of this world are clever in their dealings with one another; Jesus' followers should be as wise in their own way.

decisions.choice: {{gender:children|sons}}
decisions.reason: The phrase means people of both sexes, as in 6:35.

decisions.choice: the people of this age; the people of the light (B); people who belong to this world; people who belong to the light (R)
alternatives: sons of this age; sons of the light
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the meaning of the idiom.

decisions.choice: When the master heard about it
decisions.reason: Readable supplies how the master came to know, which the story implies.

decisions.choice: sagazmente, más sagaces (L); sagacidad, sagaz (B); listo (R)
decisions.reason: The word is practical wisdom that thinks ahead (meaning decision m3). The term sheet's "prudente" fits the wise servants of the parables; here a dishonest man is praised for his foresight, and "sagaz" says that cleverness without approving what he did.

decisions.choice: los hijos, with no gender span
decisions.reason: The English Literal offers "sons" as the traditional form of "children". Spanish "hijos" already covers sons and daughters, so the setting has nothing to change.

decisions.choice: kwa werevu, werevu zaidi (L, B); werevu, wana akili zaidi (R)
decisions.reason: The word is practical wisdom that thinks ahead (meaning decision m3). The term sheet's "busara" fits the wise servants of the parables; here a dishonest man is praised for his foresight, and "werevu" (shrewdness) says that cleverness without calling him wise.

decisions.choice: wana, with no gender span
decisions.reason: The English Literal offers "sons" as the traditional form of "children". Swahili "wana" already means sons and daughters, so the setting has nothing to change.

source.text: καὶ ἐγὼ ὑμῖν λέγω, ἑαυτοῖς ποιήσατε φίλους ἐκ τοῦ μαμωνᾶ τῆς ἀδικίας, ἵνα ὅταν ἐκλίπῃ δέξωνται ὑμᾶς εἰς τὰς αἰωνίους σκηνάς.

records.literal_gloss: And I to you say, for yourselves make friends by the mammon of unrighteousness, that when it fails they might receive you into the eternal dwellings.

en.L: And I say to you, make friends for yourselves by means of the mammon of unrighteousness, so that when it fails they may receive you into the eternal dwellings.
en.B: And I tell you, use the wealth of this unjust world to make friends for yourselves, so that when it is gone, they will welcome you into the eternal homes.
en.R: I tell you, use the money of this unfair world to make friends for yourselves. Then when your money is gone, you will be welcomed into eternal homes.

es.L: Y yo {{plural_you:les|os}} digo: {{plural_you:háganse|haceos}} amigos por medio del Mamón de la injusticia, para que, cuando se acabe, {{plural_you:los|os}} reciban en las tiendas eternas.
es.B: Y {{plural_you:les|os}} digo: {{plural_you:usen|usad}} el dinero de este mundo injusto para {{plural_you:ganarse|ganaros}} amigos, para que, cuando ese dinero se acabe, {{plural_you:los|os}} reciban en los hogares eternos.
es.R: {{plural_you:Les|Os}} digo: {{plural_you:usen|usad}} el dinero de este mundo injusto para hacer amigos. Así, cuando se {{plural_you:les|os}} acabe el dinero, {{plural_you:serán recibidos|seréis recibidos}} en hogares eternos.

fr.L: Et moi, je vous dis : faites-vous des amis au moyen du mammon d’injustice, afin que, lorsqu’il viendra à manquer, ils vous reçoivent dans les demeures éternelles.
fr.B: Et moi, je vous le dis : servez-vous de la richesse de ce monde injuste pour vous faire des amis, afin que, lorsqu’elle aura disparu, ils vous accueillent dans les demeures éternelles.
fr.R: Je vous le dis, utilisez l’argent de ce monde injuste pour vous faire des amis. Alors, quand vous n’aurez plus d’argent, vous serez accueillis dans des maisons éternelles.

sw.L: Nami nawaambia, jitengenezeeni marafiki kwa njia ya Mamona ya udhalimu, ili itakapokoma wawapokee ndani ya maskani ya milele.
sw.B: Nami nawaambia, tumieni mali ya ulimwengu huu usio wa haki kujipatia marafiki, ili mali hiyo itakapokwisha, wawakaribishe katika maskani ya milele.
sw.R: Nawaambia, tumieni mali ya ulimwengu huu usio wa haki ili mpate marafiki. Kisha mali yenu itakapokwisha, mtakaribishwa katika nyumba za milele.

decisions.choice: mammon: wealth, money and possessions
alternatives: a god or demon named Mammon
decisions.reason: The word is Aramaic for wealth or what a person owns. In 16:13 it is pictured as a master who competes with God, but it is not the name of a god.

decisions.choice: the mammon of unrighteousness: wealth that belongs to this unjust world
decisions.reason: As with "the manager of unrighteousness" (16:8), the phrase is a Hebrew way of describing. Wealth easily leads people into wrong and belongs to this passing age, unlike the true riches of 16:11. Jesus does not mean only money gained dishonestly.

decisions.choice: when it fails: when wealth runs out or comes to an end, at death or at the end of this age
decisions.reason: The subject is the wealth. Like the manager's position, money will not last.

decisions.choice: when it fails (SBLGNT)
alternatives: when you fail, that is, when you die
decisions.reason: The earliest manuscripts read "when it fails". Many later manuscripts read "when you fail", meaning when you die. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: they may receive you: the friends made by generous giving, or God
decisions.reason: The friends are the poor who have been helped (compare 12:33; 14:13-14). The plural can also be a reverent way of speaking of God's action, as in 12:20.

decisions.choice: the eternal dwellings: homes in the life of the age to come
decisions.reason: The word means tents or dwellings. In contrast to the homes the manager hoped for (16:4), these last forever.

decisions.choice: mammon (L); wealth (B); money (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "mammon", the Aramaic word for wealth that the Greek itself borrows. Balanced says "wealth" and Readable "money", the everyday words for it.

decisions.choice: of this unjust world (B); of this unfair world (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the meaning of the Hebrew-style phrase, as the meaning decision explains.

decisions.choice: you will be welcomed
decisions.reason: Readable leaves the welcomers unnamed, as the Greek leaves them unclear.

decisions.choice: plural_you spans on every plural "you" ({{plural_you:les|os}}, {{plural_you:háganse|haceos}})
decisions.reason: Jesus turns from the story to his hearers, so each plural "you", pronoun or verb, is a reader setting: ustedes (Latin America, the default) or vosotros (Spain). The same through this chapter.

decisions.choice: Mamón (L), capitalized; el dinero (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Aramaic word for wealth (meaning decision m1), as the English does; the capital makes it read as the name of a master, as in 16:13. Balanced and Readable say "el dinero", as the term sheet sets. The same in 16:11 and 16:13.

decisions.choice: le mammon (L); la richesse (B); l’argent (R)
decisions.reason: As the English: Literal keeps the borrowed word, which French dictionaries list in lower case as a noun for wealth; a capital would make it a proper name before 16:13 pictures it as a master. Balanced and Readable say what it means (m1).

decisions.choice: Mamona (L); mali (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Aramaic word for wealth (meaning decision m1), as the English does. Balanced and Readable say "mali" (wealth, possessions), as the term sheet sets. The same in 16:11 and 16:13.

source.text: Ὁ πιστὸς ἐν ἐλαχίστῳ καὶ ἐν πολλῷ πιστός ἐστιν, καὶ ὁ ἐν ἐλαχίστῳ ἄδικος καὶ ἐν πολλῷ ἄδικός ἐστιν.

records.literal_gloss: The [one] faithful with very little also with much faithful is, and the [one] with very little unrighteous also with much unrighteous is.

en.L: The one faithful in very little is also faithful in much, and the one unrighteous in very little is also unrighteous in much.
en.B: Someone who is faithful in the smallest matter is faithful in large matters too, and someone who is dishonest in the smallest matter is dishonest in large matters too.
en.R: If people can be trusted with small things, they can be trusted with big things too. If people are dishonest with small things, they will be dishonest with big things too.

es.L: El que es fiel en lo mínimo es fiel también en lo mucho, y el que es injusto en lo mínimo es injusto también en lo mucho.
es.B: Quien es fiel en lo más pequeño también lo es en lo grande, y quien es deshonesto en lo más pequeño también lo es en lo grande.
es.R: Si alguien es de confianza en las cosas pequeñas, también lo será en las grandes. Si alguien es deshonesto en las cosas pequeñas, también lo será en las grandes.

fr.L: Celui qui est fidèle dans très peu est aussi fidèle dans beaucoup, et celui qui est injuste dans très peu est aussi injuste dans beaucoup.
fr.B: Celui qui est fidèle dans les plus petites choses l’est aussi dans les grandes, et celui qui est malhonnête dans les plus petites choses l’est aussi dans les grandes.
fr.R: Si on peut faire confiance à quelqu’un pour de petites choses, on peut aussi lui faire confiance pour de grandes choses. Si quelqu’un est malhonnête pour de petites choses, il sera malhonnête aussi pour de grandes choses.

sw.L: Mwaminifu katika jambo dogo kabisa ni mwaminifu pia katika mengi, naye dhalimu katika jambo dogo kabisa ni dhalimu pia katika mengi.
sw.B: Mtu mwaminifu katika jambo dogo kabisa ni mwaminifu pia katika mambo makubwa, na mtu mdanganyifu katika jambo dogo kabisa ni mdanganyifu pia katika mambo makubwa.
sw.R: Watu wanaoweza kuaminiwa katika mambo madogo wanaweza kuaminiwa pia katika mambo makubwa. Watu wanaodanganya katika mambo madogo watadanganya pia katika mambo makubwa.

decisions.choice: faithful: reliable, able to be trusted
decisions.reason: The word describes someone who does what is entrusted to him, as in 12:42.

decisions.choice: unrighteous: dishonest, unjust
decisions.reason: The opposite of faithful here. It picks up the "manager of unrighteousness" (16:8).

decisions.choice: a general saying about character
decisions.reason: How a person handles small things shows how he will handle great ones. The next verses apply it to wealth.

decisions.choice: can be trusted
decisions.reason: Readable uses the everyday meaning of the word.

source.text: εἰ οὖν ἐν τῷ ἀδίκῳ μαμωνᾷ πιστοὶ οὐκ ἐγένεσθε, τὸ ἀληθινὸν τίς ὑμῖν πιστεύσει;

records.literal_gloss: If therefore in the unrighteous mammon faithful not you have been, the true [riches] who to you will entrust?

en.L: If, then, you have not been faithful with the unrighteous mammon, who will entrust the true [riches] to you?
en.B: So if you have not been faithful in handling unjust wealth, who will put real wealth in your care?
en.R: So if you cannot be trusted with the money of this unfair world, who will trust you with the riches that really matter?

es.L: Si, pues, con el Mamón injusto no {{plural_you:han sido|habéis sido}} fieles, la [riqueza] verdadera, ¿quién {{plural_you:se la|os la}} confiará?
es.B: Así que, si no {{plural_you:han sido|habéis sido}} fieles en el manejo del dinero injusto, ¿quién {{plural_you:les|os}} confiará la riqueza verdadera?
es.R: Así que, si no se puede confiar en {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} con el dinero de este mundo injusto, ¿quién {{plural_you:les|os}} confiará las riquezas que de verdad valen?

fr.L: Si donc vous n’avez pas été fidèles dans le mammon injuste, qui vous confiera le véritable [bien] ?
fr.B: Si donc vous n’avez pas été dignes de confiance dans l’usage de la richesse injuste, qui vous confiera la vraie richesse ?
fr.R: Alors, si on ne peut pas vous faire confiance avec l’argent de ce monde injuste, qui vous confiera les richesses qui comptent vraiment ?

sw.L: Basi ikiwa katika Mamona dhalimu hamkuwa waaminifu, [utajiri] wa kweli ni nani atakayewakabidhi?
sw.B: Basi kama hamkuwa waaminifu katika kutumia mali isiyo ya haki, ni nani atakayewakabidhi utajiri wa kweli?
sw.R: Kwa hiyo kama hamwezi kuaminiwa na mali ya ulimwengu huu usio wa haki, ni nani atakayewaamini na utajiri ulio wa thamani kweli?

decisions.choice: will entrust: will put in your care
decisions.reason: The verb usually means to believe or trust in. With an object handed over, it means to entrust something to someone.

decisions.choice: the true riches: what has real and lasting worth, the riches of God's kingdom
decisions.reason: The word means true or real, in contrast to wealth that passes away (12:33).

decisions.choice: the unrighteous mammon: wealth that belongs to this unjust world
decisions.reason: As in 16:9.

decisions.choice: mammon (L); wealth (B); money (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "mammon", the Aramaic word for wealth that the Greek itself borrows. Balanced says "wealth" and Readable "money", the everyday words for it.

decisions.choice: entrust (L); put in your care (B); trust you with (R)
decisions.reason: The verb here means to entrust, as the meaning decision explains.

decisions.choice: [riches] (L); wealth (B); riches (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek says only "the true"; the context supplies the noun.

source.text: καὶ εἰ ἐν τῷ ἀλλοτρίῳ πιστοὶ οὐκ ἐγένεσθε, τὸ ὑμέτερον τίς δώσει ὑμῖν;

records.literal_gloss: And if in that which [is] another's faithful not you have been, that which [is] yours who will give to you?

en.L: And if you have not been faithful with what belongs to another, who will give you what is yours?
en.B: And if you have not proved faithful with what is another's, who will hand you what is your own?
en.R: And if you cannot be trusted with things that belong to someone else, who will give you things of your own?

es.L: Y si con lo ajeno no {{plural_you:han sido|habéis sido}} fieles, {{plural_you:lo de ustedes|lo vuestro}}, ¿quién {{plural_you:se lo|os lo}} dará?
es.B: Y si no {{plural_you:han demostrado|habéis demostrado}} ser fieles con lo que es de otro, ¿quién {{plural_you:les|os}} entregará lo que es {{plural_you:de ustedes|vuestro}}?
es.R: Y si no se puede confiar en {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} con lo que pertenece a otra persona, ¿quién {{plural_you:les|os}} dará algo que sea {{plural_you:de ustedes|vuestro}}?

fr.L: Et si vous n’avez pas été fidèles dans ce qui est à autrui, qui vous donnera ce qui est à vous ?
fr.B: Et si vous ne vous êtes pas montrés fidèles avec le bien d’autrui, qui vous remettra le vôtre ?
fr.R: Et si on ne peut pas vous faire confiance avec des choses qui appartiennent à quelqu’un d’autre, qui vous donnera des choses à vous ?

sw.L: Na ikiwa katika kilicho cha mwingine hamkuwa waaminifu, kilicho chenu ni nani atakayewapa?
sw.B: Na kama hamkuonyesha uaminifu katika mali ya mtu mwingine, ni nani atakayewakabidhi kilicho chenu?
sw.R: Na kama hamwezi kuaminiwa na vitu vya mtu mwingine, ni nani atakayewapa vitu vyenu wenyewe?

decisions.choice: what belongs to another: wealth in this life, held in trust from God
decisions.reason: Like the manager, people only manage what they have for a time. Their own lasting riches are still to come.

decisions.choice: yours (SBLGNT)
decisions.reason: Most manuscripts read "yours". A few, among them Codex Vaticanus, read "ours", which would mean the riches that belong to God and Jesus. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

source.text: οὐδεὶς οἰκέτης δύναται δυσὶ κυρίοις δουλεύειν· ἢ γὰρ τὸν ἕνα μισήσει καὶ τὸν ἕτερον ἀγαπήσει, ἢ ἑνὸς ἀνθέξεται καὶ τοῦ ἑτέρου καταφρονήσει.

records.literal_gloss: No household servant is able two masters to serve, either for the one he will hate and the other he will love, or one he will be devoted to and the other he will despise.

en.L: No household servant can serve two masters as a slave; for either {{gender:they|he}} will hate the one and love the other, or {{gender:they|he}} will hold to one and despise the other.
en.B: No servant in a household can serve two masters. Either the servant will hate one master and love the other, or be loyal to one and look down on the other.
en.R: A servant cannot serve two masters at the same time. That servant will hate one master and love the other. Or the servant will be loyal to one and not care about the other.

es.L: Ningún criado de casa puede servir como esclavo a dos señores; porque o bien odiará al uno y amará al otro, o bien se apegará a uno y despreciará al otro.
es.B: Ningún criado de una casa puede servir a dos amos. O el criado odiará a uno y amará al otro, o será leal a uno y menospreciará al otro.
es.R: Un criado no puede servir a dos amos al mismo tiempo. Odiará a uno y amará al otro. O será fiel a uno y no le importará el otro.

fr.L: Aucun domestique ne peut servir en esclave deux maîtres ; car ou bien il haïra l’un et aimera l’autre, ou bien il s’attachera à l’un et méprisera l’autre.
fr.B: Aucun serviteur d’une maison ne peut servir deux maîtres. Ou bien ce serviteur détestera l’un et aimera l’autre, ou bien il sera fidèle à l’un et méprisera l’autre.
fr.R: Un serviteur ne peut pas servir deux maîtres à la fois. Ce serviteur détestera l’un des maîtres et aimera l’autre. Ou bien il sera fidèle à l’un et ne se souciera pas de l’autre.

sw.L: Hakuna mtumishi wa nyumbani awezaye kuwatumikia mabwana wawili kama mtumwa; kwa maana ama atamchukia mmoja na kumpenda mwingine, ama atashikamana na mmoja na kumdharau mwingine.
sw.B: Hakuna mtumishi wa nyumbani anayeweza kuwatumikia mabwana wawili. Mtumishi huyo atamchukia mmoja na kumpenda mwingine, au atakuwa mwaminifu kwa mmoja na kumdharau mwingine.
sw.R: Mtumishi hawezi kuwatumikia mabwana wawili kwa wakati mmoja. Atamchukia mmoja na kumpenda mwingine. Au atakuwa mwaminifu kwa mmoja na kumpuuza mwingine.

decisions.choice: household servant; to serve as a slave: one who belongs to a master and works for him alone
alternatives: a hired worker who could have two employers
decisions.reason: The first word is a servant of the household, usually a slave. The verb is formed from the word for a slave. A slave belonged wholly to one owner.

decisions.choice: hate ... love: reject one and choose the other
decisions.reason: In Hebrew speech "love" and "hate" can mean choosing one over the other (Genesis 29:30-31; Malachi 1:2-3; Luke 14:26).

decisions.choice: hold to; despise: be loyal to one, and think little of the other
decisions.reason: The two verbs describe loyalty and disregard.

decisions.choice: {{gender:they|he}}
decisions.reason: The saying is about any servant, man or woman.

decisions.choice: the servant
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable repeat the noun instead of a pronoun.

decisions.choice: serve
decisions.reason: "Serve" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it for the slave words and as in Matthew 6:24; the meaning decision (m1) keeps that a slave belonged wholly to one owner, and Literal keeps "serve as a slave".

decisions.choice: criado de casa (L); criado (B, R); señores (L); amos (B, R)
decisions.reason: The noun is a household servant, and the verb a slave's service (meaning decision m1), which Literal shows with "servir como esclavo". "Criado" keeps this word apart from "siervo", used for the slave of other parables; "amo" is the master who owns a servant, as in Matthew 6:24.

decisions.choice: odiará, se apegará, with no gender span
decisions.reason: The English Literal needs "they|he". Spanish leaves the subject in the verb ending, so there is nothing for the setting to change.

decisions.choice: "il" with no gender setting (L), where the English has {{gender:they|he}}
decisions.reason: As the style guide says for generic pronouns: "il" referring back to "aucun domestique" is ordinary generic French and already covers any servant, man or woman.

decisions.choice: domestique, servir en esclave (L); serviteur, servir (B, R)
decisions.reason: As the English: the noun is the word for a household servant (m1), so Literal says "domestique" and keeps the slave verb as "servir en esclave"; Balanced and Readable say "serviteur" and "servir".

decisions.choice: mtumishi wa nyumbani (L, B); mtumishi (R); kama mtumwa (L)
decisions.reason: The noun is a household servant, and the verb a slave's service (meaning decision m1). Literal shows the second with "kama mtumwa", as the English Literal says "as a slave"; Balanced and Readable say "kuwatumikia", serve, as the English does.

source.text: οὐ δύνασθε θεῷ δουλεύειν καὶ μαμωνᾷ.

records.literal_gloss: Not you are able God to serve and mammon.

en.L: You cannot serve God and mammon as a slave serves."
en.B: You cannot serve both God and wealth."
en.R: You cannot serve God and money at the same time."

es.L: No {{plural_you:pueden|podéis}} servir como esclavos a Dios y a Mamón».
es.B: No {{plural_you:pueden|podéis}} servir a la vez a Dios y al dinero».
es.R: No {{plural_you:pueden|podéis}} servir a Dios y al dinero al mismo tiempo».

fr.L: Vous ne pouvez pas servir en esclaves Dieu et le mammon. »
fr.B: Vous ne pouvez pas servir à la fois Dieu et la richesse. »
fr.R: Vous ne pouvez pas servir Dieu et l’argent en même temps. »

sw.L: Hamwezi kumtumikia Mungu na Mamona kama watumwa."
sw.B: Hamwezi kumtumikia Mungu na mali pia."
sw.R: Hamwezi kumtumikia Mungu na mali kwa wakati mmoja."

decisions.choice: God and mammon: wealth pictured as a master that demands a person's loyalty
decisions.reason: Wealth is not a god, but it can rule a life as a master rules a slave. A person must choose whom to serve (12:15; 18:22-25).

decisions.choice: mammon (L); wealth (B); money (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "mammon", the Aramaic word for wealth that the Greek itself borrows. Balanced says "wealth" and Readable "money", the everyday words for it.

decisions.choice: the quotation closes here
decisions.reason: Luke's words in 16:14 interrupt Jesus' speech.

decisions.choice: serve
decisions.reason: "Serve" in Balanced and Readable, as in the first half of the saying (16:13) and in Matthew 6:24; Literal keeps "as a slave serves".

source.text: Ἤκουον δὲ ταῦτα πάντα οἱ Φαρισαῖοι φιλάργυροι ὑπάρχοντες, καὶ ἐξεμυκτήριζον αὐτόν.

records.literal_gloss: Were listening to now these things all the Pharisees, lovers of money being, and they were ridiculing him.

en.L: Now the Pharisees, being lovers of money, were listening to all these things, and they were sneering at {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: The Pharisees were listening to all this. They loved money, and they turned up their noses at {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: The Pharisees heard everything Jesus said. They loved money, so they made fun of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

es.L: Oían todas estas cosas los fariseos, que eran amantes del dinero, y se mofaban de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.B: Los fariseos escuchaban todo esto. Amaban el dinero, y se reían de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} con desdén.
es.R: Los fariseos oyeron todo lo que Jesús dijo. Amaban el dinero, así que se burlaron de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.

fr.L: Or les Pharisiens, qui aimaient l’argent, écoutaient tout cela, et ils {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} tournaient en dérision.
fr.B: Les Pharisiens écoutaient tout cela. Ils aimaient l’argent, et ils {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} regardaient de haut.
fr.R: Les Pharisiens ont entendu tout ce que Jésus disait. Ils aimaient l’argent, alors ils se sont moqués de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.

sw.L: Basi Mafarisayo, wakiwa watu wanaopenda fedha, walikuwa wakisikiliza mambo haya yote, nao wakawa wakimdhihaki.
sw.B: Mafarisayo walikuwa wakisikiliza mambo hayo yote. Walipenda fedha, nao wakambeza.
sw.R: Mafarisayo walisikia kila kitu ambacho Yesu alisema. Walipenda pesa, kwa hiyo wakamcheka kwa dharau.

decisions.choice: the Pharisees: a Jewish movement devoted to keeping the law of Moses in every part of daily life
decisions.reason: They were respected teachers among the people. They had grumbled when Jesus welcomed sinners (15:2).

decisions.choice: lovers of money: greedy
decisions.reason: The word describes a love of money, not wealth itself (2 Timothy 3:2). Jesus has just said that no one can serve both God and wealth.

decisions.choice: ridiculing: turning up the nose, sneering
decisions.reason: The verb comes from the word for a nose. It is used of the rulers mocking Jesus at the cross (23:35).

decisions.choice: turned up their noses at
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the picture in the Greek verb.

source.text: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ὑμεῖς ἐστε οἱ δικαιοῦντες ἑαυτοὺς ἐνώπιον τῶν ἀνθρώπων, ὁ δὲ θεὸς γινώσκει τὰς καρδίας ὑμῶν· ὅτι τὸ ἐν ἀνθρώποις ὑψηλὸν βδέλυγμα ἐνώπιον τοῦ θεοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: And he said to them, You are those justifying themselves before the men, but the God knows the hearts of you; for that which among men [is] exalted [is] an abomination before the God.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "You are the ones who justify yourselves before {{gender:people|men}}, but God knows your hearts; for what is exalted among {{gender:people|men}} is an abomination before God.
en.B: He said to them, "You are the ones who make yourselves out to be righteous in front of {{gender:people|men}}, but God knows your hearts. What {{gender:people|men}} think highly of is loathsome in God's sight.
en.R: Jesus said to them, "You try to make {{gender:people|men}} think you are good. But God knows what is in your hearts. The things {{gender:people|men}} think are great are the very things God hates.

es.L: Y les dijo: «{{plural_you:Ustedes son|Vosotros sois}} los que {{plural_you:se justifican a sí mismos|os justificáis a vosotros mismos}} ante {{gender:la gente|los hombres}}, pero Dios conoce {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} corazones; porque lo que entre {{gender:la gente|los hombres}} es alto, ante Dios es cosa abominable.
es.B: Él les dijo: «{{plural_you:Ustedes son|Vosotros sois}} los que {{plural_you:se hacen pasar|os hacéis pasar}} por justos ante {{gender:la gente|los hombres}}, pero Dios {{plural_you:les|os}} conoce el corazón. Lo que {{gender:la gente tiene|los hombres tienen}} en gran estima es repugnante a los ojos de Dios.
es.R: Jesús les dijo: «{{plural_you:Ustedes tratan|Vosotros tratáis}} de hacer creer a {{gender:la gente|los hombres}} que {{plural_you:son|sois}} buenos. Pero Dios sabe lo que hay en {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} corazón. Las cosas que {{gender:la gente considera|los hombres consideran}} grandes son precisamente las que Dios aborrece.

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur dit : « C’est vous qui vous justifiez vous-mêmes devant les {{gender:humains|hommes}}, mais Dieu connaît vos cœurs ; car ce qui est élevé parmi les {{gender:humains|hommes}} est une abomination devant Dieu.
fr.B: Il leur dit : « Vous, vous vous faites passer pour justes aux yeux des {{gender:gens|hommes}}, mais Dieu connaît vos cœurs. Ce que les {{gender:gens|hommes}} placent très haut, Dieu l’a en horreur.
fr.R: Jésus leur a dit : « Vous essayez de faire croire aux {{gender:gens|hommes}} que vous êtes bons. Mais Dieu sait ce qu’il y a dans vos cœurs. Les choses que les {{gender:gens|hommes}} trouvent grandes, ce sont justement celles que Dieu déteste.

sw.L: Naye akawaambia, "Ninyi ndinyi mnaojifanya wenye haki mbele ya watu, lakini Mungu anaifahamu mioyo yenu; kwa sababu kilicho juu kati ya watu ni machukizo mbele ya Mungu.
sw.B: Aliwaambia, "Ninyi ndinyi mnaojionyesha kuwa wenye haki machoni pa watu, lakini Mungu anaijua mioyo yenu. Kile ambacho watu wanakithamini sana ni kitu cha kuchukiza machoni pa Mungu.
sw.R: Yesu aliwaambia, "Mnajaribu kuwafanya watu wawaone kuwa wema. Lakini Mungu anajua yaliyomo mioyoni mwenu. Mambo ambayo watu wanayaona kuwa makubwa ndiyo hasa yale ambayo Mungu anayachukia.

decisions.choice: justify yourselves: show yourselves to be in the right, make yourselves look righteous
decisions.reason: They seek to be seen as righteous by others (10:29; 18:9-14). God, who sees the heart, judges differently.

decisions.choice: God knows your hearts: the God who looks on the heart
decisions.reason: Scripture says that people look at outward appearance, but the Lord looks at the heart (1 Samuel 16:7; Proverbs 21:2).

decisions.choice: abomination: something God finds disgusting
decisions.reason: The word is used in the Greek Old Testament for what the Lord hates, such as idols and the pride of the arrogant (Proverbs 16:5).

decisions.choice: exalted: high, prized, admired
decisions.reason: What people prize, such as wealth and a good name, can be the very thing God rejects (1:51-53).

decisions.choice: {{gender:people|men}}
decisions.reason: The word means human beings in general.

decisions.choice: the quotation opens here and runs on to 16:31
decisions.reason: Jesus' words from 16:15 to the end of the chapter are one speech.

decisions.choice: {{gender:la gente|los hombres}}, with the verb inside the span where it agrees ({{gender:la gente tiene|los hombres tienen}})
decisions.reason: As the English: the Greek word means people in general here. "La gente" is the inclusive default and "los hombres" the traditional wording; "la gente" takes a singular verb, so the verb goes inside the span.

decisions.choice: « opens here and closes at the end of 16:31; Abraham's and the rich man's words are in “ ”
decisions.reason: Jesus' words run on to the end of the chapter, as in the English, with the speech inside the story in the second level of quotation marks.

decisions.choice: vous justifiez vous-mêmes (L); vous vous faites passer pour justes (B)
decisions.reason: The term sheet's "déclarer juste" is for God's verdict; here people make themselves look righteous before others (m1), so Balanced says that. Literal keeps "justifier", whose French sense of defending oneself is close to the point.

decisions.choice: watu, with no gender span
decisions.reason: The English offers "people" with "men" as the traditional form. Swahili "watu" already means people of either sex, and "wanaume" would mean only males, so the setting has nothing to change.

source.text: Ὁ νόμος καὶ οἱ προφῆται μέχρι Ἰωάννου· ἀπὸ τότε ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ εὐαγγελίζεται καὶ πᾶς εἰς αὐτὴν βιάζεται.

records.literal_gloss: The law and the prophets [were] until John; from that time the kingdom of the God is proclaimed and everyone into it forces his way.

en.L: The law and the prophets [were] until John; from that time the kingdom of God is proclaimed as good news, and everyone is forcing [a way] into it.
en.B: The law and the prophets lasted until John. From then on, the kingdom of God is announced as good news, and everyone is pressing their way into it.
en.R: The law of Moses and the writings of the prophets were God's message until John came. Since then, the good news about the kingdom of God is being told. And people are pushing hard to get into it.

es.L: La ley y los profetas [fueron] hasta Juan; desde entonces el reino de Dios se anuncia como buena noticia, y cada uno se abre paso a la fuerza hacia él.
es.B: La ley y los profetas llegaron hasta Juan. Desde entonces se anuncia la buena noticia del reino de Dios, y todos se abren paso con fuerza para entrar en él.
es.R: La ley de Moisés y los escritos de los profetas fueron el mensaje de Dios hasta que vino Juan. Desde entonces se está dando a conocer la buena noticia del reino de Dios. Y la gente se esfuerza mucho por entrar en él.

fr.L: La Loi et les prophètes [ont été] jusqu’à Jean ; depuis lors, le royaume de Dieu est annoncé comme une bonne nouvelle, et chacun s’y introduit de force.
fr.B: La Loi et les prophètes ont duré jusqu’à Jean. Depuis, le royaume de Dieu est annoncé comme une bonne nouvelle, et chacun fait effort pour y entrer.
fr.R: La Loi de Moïse et les écrits des prophètes ont été le message de Dieu jusqu’à la venue de Jean. Depuis ce moment-là, on annonce la bonne nouvelle du royaume de Dieu. Et les gens font de grands efforts pour y entrer.

sw.L: Sheria na manabii [vilidumu] mpaka Yohana; tangu hapo ufalme wa Mungu unahubiriwa kama habari njema, na kila mtu analazimisha [njia ya] kuingia ndani yake.
sw.B: Sheria na manabii vilidumu mpaka wakati wa Yohana. Tangu hapo ufalme wa Mungu unahubiriwa kama habari njema, na kila mtu anajitahidi kwa nguvu kuingia ndani yake.
sw.R: Sheria ya Musa na maandiko ya manabii yalikuwa ujumbe wa Mungu mpaka Yohana alipokuja. Tangu wakati huo habari njema ya ufalme wa Mungu inahubiriwa. Na watu wanajitahidi sana kuingia ndani yake.

decisions.choice: the law and the prophets: the Scriptures of Israel
decisions.reason: The phrase names the whole Old Testament by two of its parts (24:27, 44).

decisions.choice: until John; from that time: John stands at the turn from the time of promise to the time of the kingdom
decisions.reason: The law and the prophets pointed ahead to what has now come (7:26-28). The next verse shows that the law has not lost its force.

decisions.choice: everyone is forcing a way into it: people press hard to enter
alternatives: everyone is urged to enter it
decisions.reason: The verb means to use force. It may describe the eagerness of those who enter (13:24), or, taken as a passive, people being urged to come in (14:23). Others take it of violent opposition. Matthew 11:12 has a related saying.

decisions.choice: is proclaimed as good news: is announced as news of salvation
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for the good news Jesus brings (4:18, 43; 8:1).

decisions.choice: [were]; [a way]
decisions.reason: Literal supplies the verb and the object English needs.

decisions.choice: were God's message until John came
decisions.reason: Readable supplies what the law and the prophets were, as the meaning decisions explain.

decisions.choice: se anuncia como buena noticia (L); se anuncia la buena noticia (B); se está dando a conocer la buena noticia (R)
decisions.reason: The verb is to announce good news (meaning decision m4). "Anunciar la buena noticia" is the wording used for it through the Gospels; "se predica" would lose the good news in the verb.

decisions.choice: unahubiriwa kama habari njema (L, B); habari njema ... inahubiriwa (R)
decisions.reason: The verb is to announce good news (meaning decision m4). "Kuhubiri habari njema" is the wording used for it through the Gospels, so the good news stays in the sentence at every level.

source.text: Εὐκοπώτερον δέ ἐστιν τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ τὴν γῆν παρελθεῖν ἢ τοῦ νόμου μίαν κεραίαν πεσεῖν.

records.literal_gloss: Easier however it is the heaven and the earth to pass away than of the law one stroke of a pen to fail.

en.L: But it is easier for heaven and earth to pass away than for one stroke of the law to fall.
en.B: Yet heaven and earth will pass away more easily than one tiny stroke of the law will fall away.
en.R: But the whole world, heaven and earth, could more easily come to an end than the smallest part of the law could fail.

es.L: Pero es más fácil que el cielo y la tierra pasen que el que caiga un solo trazo de la ley.
es.B: Sin embargo, es más fácil que el cielo y la tierra dejen de existir que el que caiga el más pequeño trazo de la ley.
es.R: Sería más fácil que todo el mundo, el cielo y la tierra, llegara a su fin, que fallara la parte más pequeña de la ley.

fr.L: Or il est plus facile au ciel et à la terre de passer qu’à un seul trait de la Loi de tomber.
fr.B: Le ciel et la terre disparaîtront plus facilement que ne tombera le moindre petit trait de la Loi.
fr.R: Le ciel et la terre, le monde entier, pourraient disparaître. Mais il est encore plus difficile que la plus petite partie de la Loi perde sa force.

sw.L: Lakini ni rahisi zaidi mbingu na dunia kupita kuliko kistari kimoja cha sheria kuanguka.
sw.B: Hata hivyo, ni rahisi zaidi mbingu na dunia kutoweka kuliko kistari kidogo kabisa cha sheria kupoteza nguvu yake.
sw.R: Ingekuwa rahisi zaidi kwa ulimwengu wote, yaani mbingu na dunia, kufikia mwisho kuliko sehemu ndogo kabisa ya sheria kushindwa.

decisions.choice: stroke: a tiny mark that tells one letter from another
decisions.reason: The word means a little horn or hook, the small stroke on a letter. Not the least part of God's law will fail (Matthew 5:18).

decisions.choice: heaven and earth: the whole created world
alternatives: the sky and the ground only
decisions.reason: The pair names everything God has made (Genesis 1:1; Luke 21:33).

decisions.choice: to fall: to fail, to lose its force
decisions.reason: A word that falls is one that is not fulfilled or no longer holds.

decisions.choice: the smallest part
decisions.reason: Readable gives the meaning of the picture.

decisions.choice: trazo
decisions.reason: The word is the small mark of the pen that tells one letter from another (meaning decision m1). "Tilde" is the familiar word, but in Spanish it names an accent mark; "trazo" is the stroke itself.

decisions.choice: kistari
decisions.reason: The word is the small mark of the pen that tells one letter from another (meaning decision m1). "Kistari" (a small stroke) says that; "nukta" is a dot.

source.text: Πᾶς ὁ ἀπολύων τὴν γυναῖκα αὐτοῦ καὶ γαμῶν ἑτέραν μοιχεύει, καὶ ὁ ἀπολελυμένην ἀπὸ ἀνδρὸς γαμῶν μοιχεύει.

records.literal_gloss: Everyone putting away the wife of him and marrying another commits adultery, and the [one] her having been put away from a husband marrying commits adultery.

en.L: Everyone who divorces his wife and marries another commits adultery, and the one who marries a woman divorced from a husband commits adultery.
en.B: Any man who divorces his wife and marries someone else is committing adultery, and the man who marries a woman her husband has divorced is committing adultery too.
en.R: If a man divorces his wife and marries another woman, he is guilty of adultery. And if a man marries a woman whose husband has divorced her, he is also guilty of adultery.

es.L: Todo el que se divorcia de su mujer y se casa con otra comete adulterio, y el que se casa con una divorciada de su marido comete adulterio.
es.B: Cualquier hombre que se divorcia de su esposa y se casa con otra mujer comete adulterio, y el hombre que se casa con una mujer de la que su marido se ha divorciado también comete adulterio.
es.R: Si un hombre se divorcia de su esposa y se casa con otra mujer, es culpable de adulterio. Y si un hombre se casa con una mujer cuyo marido se ha divorciado de ella, también es culpable de adulterio.

fr.L: Quiconque renvoie sa femme et en épouse une autre commet un adultère, et celui qui épouse une femme renvoyée par [son] mari commet un adultère.
fr.B: Tout homme qui divorce et épouse une autre femme commet un adultère, et celui qui épouse une femme dont le mari a divorcé commet lui aussi un adultère.
fr.R: Si un homme divorce et se marie avec une autre femme, il est coupable d’adultère. Et si un homme se marie avec une femme que son mari a renvoyée, il est coupable d’adultère, lui aussi.

sw.L: Kila mtu anayemtaliki mke wake na kuoa mwingine anazini, na yeye anayemwoa aliyetalikiwa na mume anazini.
sw.B: Mwanamume yeyote anayemtaliki mke wake na kuoa mwanamke mwingine anazini, na mwanamume anayemwoa mwanamke aliyetalikiwa na mumewe anazini pia.
sw.R: Mwanamume akimtaliki mke wake na kumwoa mwanamke mwingine, ana hatia ya uzinzi. Na mwanamume akimwoa mwanamke ambaye mumewe amemtaliki, yeye pia ana hatia ya uzinzi.

decisions.choice: divorces: sends away, dismisses his wife
decisions.reason: The verb means to release or send away. In Jewish law a husband could divorce his wife by giving her a written notice (Deuteronomy 24:1-4).

decisions.choice: a saying that shows the law's force: marriage stays binding before God
alternatives: a new law replacing the law of Moses
decisions.reason: After saying that not a stroke of the law will fail (16:17), Jesus gives an example where he holds people to God's purpose for marriage more strictly than common practice (Mark 10:2-12; Matthew 19:3-9).

decisions.choice: the one who marries a woman divorced: the second man also breaks the marriage bond
decisions.reason: The subject is the man who marries her. Luke gives the saying from the side of the men, who alone could divorce under the law.

decisions.choice: se divorcia de; divorciada
decisions.reason: The verb is to send a wife away, which was divorce (meaning decision m1). "Divorciarse de" is the plain modern word, as the term sheet sets; "repudiar" is older and now reads as rejecting someone.

decisions.choice: kutaliki; aliyetalikiwa
decisions.reason: The verb is to send a wife away, which was divorce (meaning decision m1). "Kutaliki" is the plain word for divorce, as the term sheet sets; "kumwacha" (to leave her) is softer and can mean simply deserting.

source.text: Ἄνθρωπος δέ τις ἦν πλούσιος, καὶ ἐνεδιδύσκετο πορφύραν καὶ βύσσον εὐφραινόμενος καθ’ ἡμέραν λαμπρῶς.

records.literal_gloss: A man now certain there was rich, and he was clothed in purple and fine linen, making good cheer every day in splendor.

en.L: Now there was a certain rich man, and he used to dress in purple and fine linen, feasting splendidly every day.
en.B: There was once a rich man who wore purple and fine linen and feasted in great style day after day.
en.R: There was once a rich man who always wore expensive purple robes and clothes made of fine linen. Every day he had grand meals and enjoyed himself.

es.L: Y cierto hombre era rico, y vestía de púrpura y lino fino, banqueteando espléndidamente cada día.
es.B: Había una vez un hombre rico que vestía ropas de púrpura y de lino fino, y que cada día daba fiestas con gran lujo.
es.R: Había una vez un hombre rico que siempre llevaba túnicas caras de color púrpura y ropa de lino fino. Cada día tenía comidas espléndidas y se divertía.

fr.L: Or il y avait un certain homme riche, qui s’habillait de pourpre et de lin fin, et faisait chaque jour de brillants festins.
fr.B: Il y avait un homme riche qui portait des vêtements de pourpre et de lin fin et qui, jour après jour, faisait de somptueux festins.
fr.R: Il y avait un homme riche qui portait toujours de beaux vêtements de pourpre très chers et des habits de lin fin. Chaque jour, il faisait de grands repas et s’amusait bien.

sw.L: Na mtu fulani alikuwa tajiri, akijivika vazi la zambarau na kitani laini, akifurahia karamu za kifahari kila siku.
sw.B: Kulikuwa na mtu tajiri ambaye alivaa mavazi ya zambarau na kitani laini, akila karamu za kifahari siku baada ya siku.
sw.R: Kulikuwa na mtu tajiri ambaye kila mara alivaa majoho ya zambarau ya bei ghali na nguo za kitani laini. Kila siku alikula vyakula vizuri sana na kujifurahisha.

decisions.choice: purple and fine linen: the clothing of kings and the very rich
decisions.reason: Purple dye came from shellfish and was very costly. Fine linen, often from Egypt, was worn next to the skin. Together they marked great wealth (Proverbs 31:22; Revelation 18:12).

decisions.choice: feasting splendidly every day: enjoying rich meals in luxury, day after day
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for the celebration of 15:23-24 and the rich fool's "be merry" (12:19). Here it is a way of life.

decisions.choice: a certain rich man: the parable begins like the one in 16:1
decisions.reason: The words "a certain rich man" open both parables of this chapter (16:1). The rich man has no name.

source.text: πτωχὸς δέ τις ὀνόματι Λάζαρος ἐβέβλητο πρὸς τὸν πυλῶνα αὐτοῦ εἱλκωμένος καὶ ἐπιθυμῶν χορτασθῆναι ἀπὸ τῶν πιπτόντων ἀπὸ τῆς τραπέζης τοῦ πλουσίου· ἀλλὰ καὶ οἱ κύνες ἐρχόμενοι ἐπέλειχον τὰ ἕλκη αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: A poor man now certain named Lazarus was laid at the gate of him being full of sores \v 21 and desiring to be fed from the [things] falling from the table of the rich man; but even the dogs coming were licking the sores of him.

en.L: And a certain poor man named Lazarus had been laid at his gate, covered with sores, \v 21 and longing to be fed from what fell from the rich man's table; but even the dogs would come and lick his sores.
en.B: And a poor man named Lazarus had been put down at his gate. His body was covered with sores, \v 21 and he longed to fill his stomach with whatever dropped from the rich man's table. Instead, the dogs would come and lick his sores.
en.R: A poor man named Lazarus was lying by the gate of the rich man's house. Someone had put him there. Lazarus had sores all over his body. \v 21 He was so hungry that he wanted to eat even the scraps of food that fell from the rich man's table. Dogs even came and licked his sores.

es.L: Y un pobre llamado Lázaro había sido tendido junto a su portón, cubierto de úlceras, \v 21 y deseando hartarse de lo que caía de la mesa del rico; pero incluso los perros venían a lamerle las úlceras.
es.B: Y a la puerta de su casa habían dejado a un pobre llamado Lázaro. Tenía el cuerpo cubierto de úlceras, \v 21 y deseaba llenarse el estómago con lo que caía de la mesa del rico. En cambio, los perros venían a lamerle las úlceras.
es.R: Un hombre pobre llamado Lázaro estaba tirado junto a la puerta de la casa del rico. Alguien lo había dejado allí. Lázaro tenía llagas por todo el cuerpo. \v 21 Tenía tanta hambre que quería comer aunque fueran las sobras que caían de la mesa del rico. Hasta los perros venían y le lamían las llagas.

fr.L: Et un pauvre, nommé Lazare, avait été couché à son portail, couvert d’ulcères, \v 21 et désireux de se rassasier de ce qui tombait de la table du riche ; mais même les chiens venaient lécher ses ulcères.
fr.B: Un pauvre, nommé Lazare, avait été déposé à son portail. Il avait le corps couvert de plaies, \v 21 et il aurait bien voulu se remplir l’estomac de ce qui tombait de la table du riche. Au lieu de cela, les chiens venaient lécher ses plaies.
fr.R: Un pauvre qui s’appelait Lazare était couché devant le portail de la maison du riche. Quelqu’un l’avait mis là. Lazare avait des plaies sur tout le corps. \v 21 Il avait si faim qu’il aurait voulu manger même les restes qui tombaient de la table du riche. Les chiens venaient même lécher ses plaies.

sw.L: Na maskini fulani aitwaye Lazaro alikuwa amelazwa penye lango lake, akiwa amejaa madonda, \v 21 na akitamani kushiba kwa vitu vilivyoanguka kutoka mezani pa tajiri; lakini hata mbwa walikuja na kulamba madonda yake.
sw.B: Na maskini mmoja aitwaye Lazaro alikuwa amewekwa langoni pake. Mwili wake ulikuwa umejaa madonda, \v 21 naye alitamani kujaza tumbo lake kwa chochote kilichoanguka kutoka mezani pa yule tajiri. Badala yake, mbwa walikuja kumlamba madonda yake.
sw.R: Maskini mmoja aitwaye Lazaro alikuwa amelala karibu na lango la nyumba ya yule tajiri. Mtu fulani alikuwa amemweka hapo. Lazaro alikuwa na vidonda mwili mzima. \v 21 Alikuwa na njaa sana hata alitamani kula makombo ya chakula yaliyoanguka kutoka mezani pa yule tajiri. Hata mbwa walikuja kulamba vidonda vyake.

decisions.choice: Lazarus: a common Jewish name, a form of Eleazar, meaning "God helps"
decisions.reason: He is the only person named in any of Jesus' parables. The name fits him: he has no one but God to help him.

decisions.choice: had been laid: placed there by others, because he could not walk or stand
decisions.reason: The verb means "thrown" or "put". Others had left him there to beg.

decisions.choice: what fell from the rich man's table (SBLGNT)
alternatives: the crumbs that fell from the rich man's table
