decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add "the crumbs", perhaps from Matthew 15:27. The earliest manuscripts do not have it. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: but even the dogs ... licked his sores: he was so helpless that stray dogs came to him
alternatives: the dogs were caring for him
decisions.reason: Dogs in the streets were scavengers and counted unclean. "But even" adds to his misery: no one fed him, and he could not keep the dogs away.

decisions.choice: Someone had put him there.
decisions.reason: Readable explains the passive, as the meaning decision explains.

decisions.choice: eat even the scraps of food
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what fell from the table.

source.text: ἐγένετο δὲ ἀποθανεῖν τὸν πτωχὸν καὶ ἀπενεχθῆναι αὐτὸν ὑπὸ τῶν ἀγγέλων εἰς τὸν κόλπον Ἀβραάμ· ἀπέθανεν δὲ καὶ ὁ πλούσιος καὶ ἐτάφη.

records.literal_gloss: It came to pass then [that] died the poor man and was carried away he by the angels into the bosom of Abraham; died then also the rich man and was buried.

en.L: And it came about that the poor man died and was carried away by the angels into Abraham's bosom; and the rich man also died and was buried.
en.B: The day came when the poor man died, and angels carried him off to be at Abraham's side. The rich man also died, and was given a burial.
en.R: Then Lazarus died, and the angels carried him away to sit close beside Abraham. The rich man died too, and people buried him.

es.L: Y sucedió que el pobre murió y fue llevado por los ángeles al regazo de Abraham; y el rico murió también y fue enterrado.
es.B: Llegó el día en que el pobre murió, y los ángeles se lo llevaron para que estuviera al lado de Abraham. El rico también murió, y recibió sepultura.
es.R: Luego Lázaro murió, y los ángeles se lo llevaron para que se sentara muy cerca de Abraham. El rico también murió, y la gente lo enterró.

fr.L: Or il est arrivé que le pauvre est mort et a été emporté par les anges dans le sein d’Abraham ; le riche aussi est mort et a été enseveli.
fr.B: Un jour, le pauvre est mort, et les anges l’ont emporté auprès d’Abraham. Le riche est mort lui aussi, et on l’a enterré.
fr.R: Puis Lazare est mort, et les anges l’ont emporté pour qu’il soit assis tout près d’Abraham. Le riche est mort lui aussi, et des gens l’ont enterré.

sw.L: Ilitokea kwamba maskini alikufa, akapelekwa na malaika hadi kifuani pa Ibrahimu; na tajiri pia alikufa, kisha akazikwa.
sw.B: Siku moja yule maskini alikufa, na malaika wakamchukua akae kando ya Ibrahimu. Tajiri naye alikufa, akafanyiwa mazishi.
sw.R: Kisha Lazaro alikufa, na malaika wakamchukua akaketi karibu kabisa na Ibrahimu. Tajiri naye alikufa, na watu wakamzika.

decisions.choice: into Abraham's bosom: to the place of honor beside Abraham
alternatives: Abraham held him like a child
decisions.reason: At a feast, guests reclined on couches, and the one closest to the host lay against his chest (John 13:23). Lazarus shares the feast of God's kingdom with Abraham, the father of Israel (13:28-29).

decisions.choice: was buried: the rich man had a proper burial, but nothing more is said
decisions.reason: Nothing is said of a burial for Lazarus, who is carried by angels. The rich man's story ends in a grave.

decisions.choice: carried by the angels: God's care for the poor man at his death
alternatives: a teaching about how every soul travels after death
decisions.reason: The parable uses pictures known from Jewish teaching of the time. Its point is the great reversal, not a map of the life after death.

decisions.choice: to be at Abraham's side (B); to sit close beside Abraham (R)
decisions.reason: "Bosom" is old-fashioned. Balanced and Readable give the sense of the picture, which Literal keeps.

decisions.choice: Lazarus
decisions.reason: Readable names him.

decisions.choice: al regazo de Abraham (L)
decisions.reason: The Greek is the bosom or lap, the place of honor beside Abraham at a meal (meaning decision m1). "Regazo" keeps the picture in present-day Spanish; Balanced and Readable say what it means, as the English does. The same in 16:23.

source.text: καὶ ἐν τῷ ᾅδῃ ἐπάρας τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς αὐτοῦ, ὑπάρχων ἐν βασάνοις, ὁρᾷ Ἀβραὰμ ἀπὸ μακρόθεν καὶ Λάζαρον ἐν τοῖς κόλποις αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: And in the Hades having lifted up the eyes of him, being in torments, he sees Abraham from afar and Lazarus in the bosom of him.

en.L: And in Hades, lifting up his eyes, being in torment, he sees Abraham far off and Lazarus in his bosom.
en.B: From Hades, in the midst of his torment, he raised his eyes and saw Abraham a long way off, and Lazarus close beside him.
en.R: The rich man went to the place of the dead and was in great pain there. He looked up and saw Abraham far away, with Lazarus right next to him.

es.L: Y en el Hades, levantando los ojos, mientras estaba en tormentos, ve a Abraham desde lejos y a Lázaro en su regazo.
es.B: Desde el Hades, en medio de su tormento, levantó la vista y vio a Abraham a lo lejos, y a Lázaro junto a él.
es.R: El rico fue al lugar de los muertos y allí sufría mucho dolor. Miró hacia arriba y vio a Abraham muy lejos, con Lázaro a su lado.

fr.L: Et dans l’Hadès, levant les yeux, étant dans les tourments, il voit Abraham de loin, et Lazare dans son sein.
fr.B: Du séjour des morts, au milieu de ses tourments, il a levé les yeux et a vu de loin Abraham, et Lazare tout près de lui.
fr.R: Le riche est allé au séjour des morts, et là, il souffrait beaucoup. Il a levé les yeux et il a vu Abraham, très loin, avec Lazare juste à côté de lui.

sw.L: Na huko Kuzimu, alipoinua macho yake, huku akiteseka, anamwona Ibrahimu kwa mbali, na Lazaro kifuani pake.
sw.B: Kutoka Kuzimu, akiwa katikati ya mateso yake, aliinua macho akamwona Ibrahimu mbali sana, na Lazaro karibu naye.
sw.R: Tajiri alikwenda Kuzimu, akawa na maumivu makali huko. Alitazama juu akamwona Ibrahimu mbali sana, na Lazaro alikuwa karibu kabisa naye.

decisions.choice: Hades: the place of the dead
decisions.reason: The Greek Old Testament uses the word for Sheol, the world of the dead (10:15; Acts 2:27). Here it is a place of torment for the rich man, separated from the place where Lazarus is. It is a different word from Gehenna (12:5).

decisions.choice: torment: severe pain
decisions.reason: The word is used of torture and severe pain (Matthew 4:24). 16:24 speaks of a flame.

decisions.choice: he sees: a vivid present in the middle of the story
decisions.reason: The storyteller switches to the present tense to make the scene come alive.

decisions.choice: saw (B, R); sees (L)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable keep the past tense of the story.

decisions.choice: the place of the dead
decisions.reason: Readable explains Hades, as in 10:15.

decisions.choice: close beside him (B); right next to him (R)
decisions.reason: As in 16:22.

decisions.choice: el Hades (L, B); el lugar de los muertos (R)
decisions.reason: Hades is the place of the dead (meaning decision m1). Literal and Balanced keep the name, as the English does; Readable says what it is. "El infierno" is kept for Gehenna.

decisions.choice: ve (L); vio (B, R)
decisions.reason: As the English: Luke tells this in a vivid present (meaning decision m3). Literal keeps it; Balanced and Readable tell the story in the past.

decisions.choice: l’Hadès (L); le séjour des morts (B, R)
decisions.reason: The term sheet's forms, as in 10:15: the word names the place of the dead (m1), and "l’enfer" would say more than the Greek. Literal keeps the present "il voit" (m3).

decisions.choice: Kuzimu at every level
decisions.reason: Hades is the place of the dead (meaning decision m1). "Kuzimu" is the Swahili word for the world of the dead, so Readable needs no explanation where the English Readable says "the place of the dead"; "jehanamu" is kept for Gehenna.

decisions.choice: anamwona (L); akamwona (B, R)
decisions.reason: As the English: Luke tells this in a vivid present (meaning decision m3). Literal keeps it; Balanced and Readable use the narrative past, with -li- for the first verb and -ka- for those that follow.

source.text: καὶ αὐτὸς φωνήσας εἶπεν· Πάτερ Ἀβραάμ, ἐλέησόν με καὶ πέμψον Λάζαρον ἵνα βάψῃ τὸ ἄκρον τοῦ δακτύλου αὐτοῦ ὕδατος καὶ καταψύξῃ τὴν γλῶσσάν μου, ὅτι ὀδυνῶμαι ἐν τῇ φλογὶ ταύτῃ.

records.literal_gloss: And he having cried out said, Father Abraham, have mercy on me and send Lazarus that he might dip the tip of the finger of him in water and cool the tongue of me, for I am suffering in the flame this.

en.L: And he called out and said, 'Father Abraham, have mercy on me and send Lazarus so that he may dip the tip of his finger in water and cool my tongue, for I am in agony in this flame.'
en.B: So he shouted, 'Father Abraham, show me mercy! Send Lazarus here. Let him wet the end of his finger with water and cool my tongue, for this flame is causing me terrible pain.'
en.R: So he called out, 'Father Abraham, please be kind to me! Send Lazarus to me. Let him put the end of his finger in some water and cool my tongue with it. I am suffering terribly in this fire!'

es.L: Y él, alzando la voz, dijo: “Padre Abraham, ten piedad de mí y manda a Lázaro a que moje en agua la punta de su dedo y me refresque la lengua, porque sufro terriblemente en esta llama”.
es.B: Entonces gritó: “¡Padre Abraham, ten piedad de mí! Manda aquí a Lázaro. Que moje en agua la punta del dedo y me refresque la lengua, porque esta llama me causa un dolor terrible”.
es.R: Entonces gritó: “¡Padre Abraham, por favor, ten compasión de mí! Mándame a Lázaro. Que meta la punta del dedo en un poco de agua y me refresque la lengua con ella. ¡Estoy sufriendo terriblemente en este fuego!”.

fr.L: Et lui, s’étant écrié, a dit : “Père Abraham, aie pitié de moi et envoie Lazare, afin qu’il trempe le bout de son doigt dans l’eau et me rafraîchisse la langue, car je souffre cruellement dans cette flamme.”
fr.B: Alors il s’est écrié : “Père Abraham, aie pitié de moi ! Envoie Lazare ici. Qu’il mouille d’eau le bout de son doigt et vienne me rafraîchir la langue, car cette flamme me fait terriblement souffrir.”
fr.R: Alors il a appelé : “Père Abraham, s’il te plaît, sois bon pour moi ! Envoie-moi Lazare. Qu’il trempe le bout de son doigt dans un peu d’eau et qu’il me rafraîchisse la langue avec. Je souffre terriblement dans ce feu !”

sw.L: Naye, akiita kwa sauti, akasema, 'Baba Ibrahimu, nihurumie, umtume Lazaro ili alowanishe kwa maji ncha ya kidole chake na kuupoza ulimi wangu, kwa sababu ninaumia vibaya katika mwali huu.'
sw.B: Basi alipaza sauti, 'Baba Ibrahimu, nihurumie! Mtume Lazaro aje hapa. Alowanishe ncha ya kidole chake kwa maji, aupoze ulimi wangu, kwa maana mwali huu unaniumiza vibaya mno.'
sw.R: Basi aliita kwa sauti, 'Baba Ibrahimu, tafadhali nihurumie! Mtume Lazaro kwangu. Aingize ncha ya kidole chake katika maji kidogo, aupoze ulimi wangu. Ninateseka vibaya katika moto huu!'

decisions.choice: Father Abraham: he claims Abraham as his ancestor
decisions.reason: Jews called Abraham their father (3:8; John 8:39). Abraham answers "child" (16:25), but being his descendant does not save the rich man.

decisions.choice: send Lazarus: he still treats Lazarus as someone to run errands for him
decisions.reason: He speaks to Abraham, not to Lazarus, and asks for Lazarus to be sent to serve him.

decisions.choice: I am in agony: in great pain and distress
decisions.reason: The verb is used of deep pain or grief (2:48; Acts 20:38).

decisions.choice: short sentences
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable break the request into short sentences.

source.text: εἶπεν δὲ Ἀβραάμ· Τέκνον, μνήσθητι ὅτι ἀπέλαβες τὰ ἀγαθά σου ἐν τῇ ζωῇ σου, καὶ Λάζαρος ὁμοίως τὰ κακά· νῦν δὲ ὧδε παρακαλεῖται σὺ δὲ ὀδυνᾶσαι.

records.literal_gloss: Said then Abraham, Child, remember that you received fully the good [things] of you in the lifetime of you, and Lazarus likewise the evil [things]; now however here he is comforted, you however are suffering.

en.L: But Abraham said, 'Child, remember that you received your good things in your lifetime, and Lazarus likewise the bad things; but now he is comforted here, and you are in agony.
en.B: But Abraham answered, 'My child, remember: while you were alive you had your good things, and Lazarus in the same way had the bad things. Now here he finds comfort, and you are suffering.
en.R: But Abraham said, 'My child, remember how you lived. You had plenty of good things in your life, and Lazarus had many bad things happen to him. Now he is comforted here, and you are in pain.

es.L: Pero dijo Abraham: “Hijo, recuerda que ya recibiste tus cosas buenas durante tu vida, y Lázaro, de igual modo, las malas; ahora, en cambio, aquí él recibe consuelo, y tú sufres.
es.B: Pero Abraham le contestó: “Hijo mío, recuerda: mientras vivías tuviste tus cosas buenas, y Lázaro, del mismo modo, las malas. Ahora él encuentra consuelo aquí, y tú sufres.
es.R: Pero Abraham le dijo: “Hijo mío, recuerda cómo viviste. Tuviste muchas cosas buenas en tu vida, y a Lázaro le pasaron muchas cosas malas. Ahora él recibe consuelo aquí, y tú sufres dolor.

fr.L: Mais Abraham a dit : “Enfant, souviens-toi que tu as reçu tes biens pendant ta vie, et Lazare de même les maux ; mais maintenant il est consolé ici, et toi, tu souffres cruellement.
fr.B: Mais Abraham a répondu : “Mon enfant, souviens-toi : de ton vivant, tu as reçu tes biens, et Lazare, de la même manière, a reçu les malheurs. Maintenant, ici, il trouve la consolation, et toi, tu souffres.
fr.R: Mais Abraham a dit : “Mon enfant, rappelle-toi comment tu as vécu. Tu as eu beaucoup de bonnes choses dans ta vie, et Lazare a eu beaucoup de malheurs. Maintenant, ici, il est consolé, et toi, tu as mal.

sw.L: Ibrahimu naye akasema, 'Mwanangu, kumbuka kwamba ulishapokea vitu vyako vizuri maishani mwako, na Lazaro, kwa namna hiyo hiyo, vitu vibaya; lakini sasa hapa yeye anafarijiwa, na wewe uko katika maumivu.
sw.B: Lakini Ibrahimu alijibu, 'Mwanangu, kumbuka: ulipokuwa hai ulikuwa na vitu vyako vizuri, na Lazaro naye alikuwa na vitu vibaya. Sasa yeye anafarijiwa hapa, na wewe unateseka.
sw.R: Lakini Ibrahimu alisema, 'Mwanangu, kumbuka jinsi ulivyoishi. Ulikuwa na vitu vingi vizuri maishani mwako, na Lazaro alipatwa na mambo mengi mabaya. Sasa yeye anafarijiwa hapa, na wewe uko katika maumivu.

decisions.choice: you received: you received in full, and have nothing more to come
decisions.reason: The verb means to receive what is due, in full. Compare 6:24, where a related verb says that the rich have already received their comfort.

decisions.choice: now he is comforted, and you are in agony: the great reversal
alternatives: a rule that all rich people suffer
decisions.reason: Mary's song (1:52-53) and the blessings and woes (6:20-26) speak of the same turning of fortunes. The rich man's fault is shown in 16:19-21: he feasted while Lazarus starved at his gate.

decisions.choice: your good things; the bad things: the rich man's good things were his own choice and possession
decisions.reason: Abraham says "your good things", but only "the bad things" of Lazarus.

decisions.choice: Abraham's words open here and run on to 16:26
decisions.reason: Abraham's answer is one speech.

source.text: καὶ ἐν πᾶσι τούτοις μεταξὺ ἡμῶν καὶ ὑμῶν χάσμα μέγα ἐστήρικται, ὅπως οἱ θέλοντες διαβῆναι ἔνθεν πρὸς ὑμᾶς μὴ δύνωνται, μηδὲ ἐκεῖθεν πρὸς ἡμᾶς διαπερῶσιν.

records.literal_gloss: And besides all these things between us and you a chasm great has been fixed, so that those desiring to pass from here to you not are able, nor from there to us can they cross over.

en.L: And besides all these things, between us and you a great chasm has been fixed, so that those who want to pass from here to you are not able, nor may they cross over from there to us.'
en.B: What is more, a vast gulf lies fixed between us and you. Anyone who wanted to go across from here to you could not, and no one can cross from your side to ours.'
en.R: Besides, there is a huge, deep gap between us and you. It is there so that no one from here can cross over to you, even if they want to. And no one from there can cross over to us.'

es.L: Y además de todo esto, entre nosotros y {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} se ha establecido un gran abismo, para que los que quieran pasar de aquí a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} no puedan, ni de allí crucen hacia nosotros”.
es.B: Y por si fuera poco, entre nosotros y {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} hay fijado un abismo inmenso. Nadie que quisiera cruzar de aquí hasta {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} podría hacerlo, y nadie puede cruzar {{plural_you:del lado de ustedes|de vuestro lado}} al nuestro”.
es.R: Además, entre nosotros y {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} hay un abismo enorme y profundo. Está ahí para que nadie de aquí pueda cruzar hasta donde {{plural_you:están ustedes|estáis vosotros}}, aunque quiera. Y nadie de allí puede cruzar hasta nosotros”.

fr.L: Et en plus de tout cela, entre nous et vous un grand abîme a été fixé, afin que ceux qui voudraient passer d’ici vers vous ne le puissent pas, et qu’on ne traverse pas non plus de là-bas vers nous.”
fr.B: De plus, un immense gouffre est établi entre nous et vous. Celui qui voudrait passer d’ici vers vous ne le pourrait pas, et personne ne peut traverser de chez vous jusqu’à nous.”
fr.R: Et puis, il y a un grand trou très profond entre nous et vous. Il est là pour que personne d’ici ne puisse aller chez vous, même s’il le veut. Et personne de là-bas ne peut venir jusqu’à nous.”

sw.L: Tena, pamoja na hayo yote, kati yetu na ninyi korongo kubwa limethibitishwa, ili wanaotaka kupita kutoka hapa kwenda kwenu wasiweze, wala wasivuke kutoka huko kuja kwetu.'
sw.B: Zaidi ya hayo, kati yetu na ninyi kuna korongo kubwa mno lililowekwa kudumu. Mtu angetaka kuvuka kutoka huku kwenda kwenu, asingeweza, wala hakuna awezaye kuvuka kutoka upande wenu kuja kwetu.'
sw.R: Tena, kati yetu na ninyi kuna korongo kubwa lenye kina kirefu. Liko hapo ili mtu yeyote wa huku asiweze kuvuka kuja kwenu, hata akitaka. Wala hakuna mtu wa huko anayeweza kuvuka kuja kwetu.'

decisions.choice: a great chasm has been fixed: a wide gap that cannot be crossed, set in place for good
decisions.reason: The verb means firmly set. The passive implies that God set it there. The choices of this life cannot be undone after death.

decisions.choice: besides all these things: in addition to what I have said
decisions.reason: Abraham gives a second reason why Lazarus cannot be sent.

decisions.choice: those who want to pass from here: even those who would like to go and help
decisions.reason: Abraham does not say that no one in his place has pity. The way is closed even to those who might want to cross.

decisions.choice: a vast gulf (B); a huge, deep gap (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use everyday words for the gap.

decisions.choice: {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}
decisions.reason: Abraham speaks to one man, but the Greek "you" here is plural: the rich man and all who are on his side of the chasm. So it takes the plural and its reader setting, while "tú" in 16:25 has none.

source.text: εἶπεν δέ· Ἐρωτῶ σε οὖν, πάτερ, ἵνα πέμψῃς αὐτὸν εἰς τὸν οἶκον τοῦ πατρός μου, ἔχω γὰρ πέντε ἀδελφούς, ὅπως διαμαρτύρηται αὐτοῖς, ἵνα μὴ καὶ αὐτοὶ ἔλθωσιν εἰς τὸν τόπον τοῦτον τῆς βασάνου.

records.literal_gloss: He said then, I implore you then, father, that you would send him to the house of the father of me, \v 28 I have for five brothers, so that he might warn them, that not also they might come to the place this of torment.

en.L: And he said, 'Then I ask you, father, to send him to my father's house, \v 28 for I have five brothers, so that he may warn them, so that they also may not come to this place of torment.'
en.B: 'Then, father, I ask you this,' he said. 'Send him to my father's house, \v 28 where I have five brothers. He can give them a solemn warning, so that they do not come to this place of torment as well.'
en.R: The rich man said, 'Then please, father, send Lazarus to my father's house. \v 28 I have five brothers there. Let Lazarus warn them, so that they will not come to this place of pain too.'

es.L: Dijo entonces: “Te pido, pues, padre, que lo mandes a la casa de mi padre, \v 28 pues tengo cinco hermanos, para que los advierta seriamente, y así tampoco ellos lleguen a este lugar de tormento”.
es.B: “Entonces, padre, te pido esto —dijo—: envíalo a la casa de mi padre, \v 28 donde tengo cinco hermanos. Que les advierta con toda seriedad, para que no vengan ellos también a este lugar de tormento”.
es.R: El rico dijo: “Entonces, por favor, padre, manda a Lázaro a la casa de mi padre. \v 28 Allí tengo cinco hermanos. Que Lázaro les avise, para que ellos no vengan también a este lugar de dolor”.

fr.L: Et il a dit : “Je te prie donc, père, de l’envoyer dans la maison de mon père, \v 28 car j’ai cinq frères, afin qu’il les avertisse solennellement, pour qu’eux aussi ne viennent pas dans ce lieu de tourment.”
fr.B: “Alors, père, je t’en supplie, a-t-il dit, envoie-le dans la maison de mon père, \v 28 où j’ai cinq frères. Qu’il les avertisse avec force, pour qu’ils ne viennent pas eux aussi dans ce lieu de tourment.”
fr.R: Le riche a dit : “Alors, père, s’il te plaît, envoie Lazare dans la maison de mon père. \v 28 J’ai cinq frères là-bas. Que Lazare les avertisse, pour qu’ils ne viennent pas eux aussi dans ce lieu de souffrance.”

sw.L: Naye akasema, 'Kwa hiyo nakusihi, baba, umpeleke katika nyumba ya baba yangu, \v 28 kwa kuwa nina ndugu watano, ili awaonye kwa dhati, wao pia wasije wakaingia katika mahali hapa pa mateso.'
sw.B: Alisema, 'Basi, baba, nakuomba jambo hili: mpeleke nyumbani kwa baba yangu, \v 28 ambako nina ndugu watano. Awaonye kwa dhati, ili wao pia wasije mahali hapa pa mateso.'
sw.R: Tajiri alisema, 'Basi, tafadhali baba, mtume Lazaro nyumbani kwa baba yangu. \v 28 Nina ndugu watano huko. Lazaro awaonye, ili wao wasije pia mahali hapa pa maumivu.'

decisions.choice: warn: testify to them, give them a solemn warning
decisions.reason: The verb means to bear witness with earnestness. In Acts it is used of the apostles' witness (Acts 2:40; 20:21).

decisions.choice: my father's house: his family, the household he grew up in
decisions.reason: "House" means the household and family.

decisions.choice: I ask you: he still asks for Lazarus to be sent on an errand
decisions.reason: As in 16:24, he speaks to Abraham about Lazarus. He now cares for his brothers, but still treats Lazarus as a messenger for his family.

decisions.choice: Lazarus
decisions.reason: Readable names the man to be sent.

source.text: λέγει δὲ Ἀβραάμ· Ἔχουσι Μωϋσέα καὶ τοὺς προφήτας· ἀκουσάτωσαν αὐτῶν.

records.literal_gloss: Says however Abraham, They have Moses and the prophets; let them hear them.

en.L: But Abraham says, 'They have Moses and the prophets; let them listen to them.'
en.B: But Abraham said, 'Moses and the prophets are there for them. Let your brothers listen to what they say.'
en.R: But Abraham said, 'Your brothers have the books that Moses and the prophets wrote. They should listen to them.'

es.L: Pero Abraham dice: “Tienen a Moisés y a los profetas; que los escuchen”.
es.B: Pero Abraham le respondió: “Ahí tienen a Moisés y a los profetas. Que tus hermanos escuchen lo que dicen”.
es.R: Pero Abraham le dijo: “Tus hermanos tienen los libros que escribieron Moisés y los profetas. Deben escucharlos”.

fr.L: Mais Abraham dit : “Ils ont Moïse et les prophètes ; qu’ils les écoutent.”
fr.B: Abraham a répondu : “Moïse et les prophètes sont là pour eux. Que tes frères écoutent ce qu’ils disent.”
fr.R: Mais Abraham a dit : “Tes frères ont les livres que Moïse et les prophètes ont écrits. Ils n’ont qu’à les écouter.”

sw.L: Lakini Ibrahimu anasema, 'Wana Musa na manabii; wawasikie hao.'
sw.B: Lakini Ibrahimu alijibu, 'Musa na manabii wapo kwa ajili yao. Ndugu zako wasikilize maneno yao.'
sw.R: Lakini Ibrahimu alisema, 'Ndugu zako wana vitabu vilivyoandikwa na Musa na manabii. Wanapaswa kuyasikiliza maandiko hayo.'

decisions.choice: Moses and the prophets: the Scriptures of Israel
decisions.reason: Moses stands for the law, the first part of the Scriptures (16:16; 24:27). They already warn against neglecting the poor (Deuteronomy 15:7-11; Isaiah 58:6-7).

decisions.choice: let them listen: let them hear and obey
decisions.reason: To listen to God's word is to do what it says (8:21; 11:28).

decisions.choice: said (B, R); says (L)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable keep the past tense of the story.

decisions.choice: the books that Moses and the prophets wrote
decisions.reason: Readable explains the phrase, as the meaning decision explains.

source.text: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· Οὐχί, πάτερ Ἀβραάμ, ἀλλ’ ἐάν τις ἀπὸ νεκρῶν πορευθῇ πρὸς αὐτοὺς μετανοήσουσιν.

records.literal_gloss: He and said, No, father Abraham, but if one from [the] dead should go to them, they will repent.

en.L: And he said, 'No, father Abraham; but if someone from the dead goes to them, they will repent.'
en.B: He answered, 'That is not enough, father Abraham. But if someone goes to them from among the dead, they will repent.'
en.R: The rich man said, 'No, father Abraham, they will not listen. But if someone comes back from the dead and goes to them, they will turn away from their sins.'

es.L: Pero él dijo: “No, padre Abraham; antes bien, si alguien de los muertos va a verlos, se arrepentirán”.
es.B: Él respondió: “Eso no basta, padre Abraham. Pero si alguien de entre los muertos va a verlos, se arrepentirán”.
es.R: El rico dijo: “No, padre Abraham, no harán caso. Pero si alguien vuelve de entre los muertos y va a verlos, se apartarán de sus pecados”.

fr.L: Et lui a dit : “Non, père Abraham ; mais si quelqu’un d’entre les morts va vers eux, ils se repentiront.”
fr.B: Il a répondu : “Cela ne suffira pas, père Abraham. Mais si quelqu’un vient à eux du milieu des morts, ils se repentiront.”
fr.R: Le riche a dit : “Non, père Abraham, ils ne vont pas écouter. Mais si quelqu’un revient de chez les morts et va les voir, ils se détourneront de leurs péchés.”

sw.L: Naye akasema, 'Sivyo, baba Ibrahimu; ila mtu fulani kutoka miongoni mwa wafu akiwaendea, watatubu.'
sw.B: Alijibu, 'Hilo halitoshi, baba Ibrahimu. Ila mtu kutoka miongoni mwa wafu akiwaendea, watatubu.'
sw.R: Tajiri alisema, 'Hapana, baba Ibrahimu, hawatasikiliza. Lakini mtu akirudi kutoka kwa wafu na kuwaendea, wataacha dhambi zao.'

decisions.choice: No: they will not listen to Moses and the prophets alone
alternatives: No, I do not agree that they have them
decisions.reason: He does not deny that they have the Scriptures; he says that will not be enough.

decisions.choice: repent: turn from sin back to God
decisions.reason: As in 15:7.

decisions.choice: That is not enough (B); they will not listen (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the "no" refers to, as the meaning decision explains.

decisions.choice: turn away from their sins
decisions.reason: Readable explains the word, as in 11:32.

decisions.choice: se arrepentirán (L, B); se apartarán de sus pecados (R)
decisions.reason: "Arrepentirse" is the word for repentance through Luke (meaning decision m2). Readable says what it means, turning away from sin, as the English Readable does and as in Luke 3:3.

decisions.choice: watatubu (L, B); wataacha dhambi zao (R)
decisions.reason: "Kutubu" is the word for repentance through Luke (meaning decision m2). Readable says what it means, turning away from sin, as the English Readable does and as in Luke 3:3.

source.text: εἶπεν δὲ αὐτῷ· Εἰ Μωϋσέως καὶ τῶν προφητῶν οὐκ ἀκούουσιν, οὐδ’ ἐάν τις ἐκ νεκρῶν ἀναστῇ πεισθήσονται.

records.literal_gloss: He said however to him, If Moses and the prophets not they hear, not even if one out from [the] dead should rise will they be persuaded.

en.L: But he said to him, 'If they do not listen to Moses and the prophets, neither will they be persuaded if someone rises from the dead.'"
en.B: Abraham said to him, 'If they will not listen to Moses and the prophets, then even someone rising from the dead will not persuade them.'"
en.R: Abraham said to him, 'If your brothers will not listen to Moses and the prophets, they will not be convinced even if someone comes back to life from the dead.'"

es.L: Pero él le dijo: “Si no escuchan a Moisés y a los profetas, tampoco se dejarán convencer aunque alguien se levante de entre los muertos”».
es.B: Abraham le respondió: “Si no hacen caso a Moisés y a los profetas, ni siquiera alguien que resucite de entre los muertos los convencerá”».
es.R: Abraham le dijo: “Si tus hermanos no escuchan a Moisés y a los profetas, tampoco se dejarán convencer aunque alguien vuelva a la vida de entre los muertos”».

fr.L: Mais il lui a dit : “S’ils n’écoutent pas Moïse et les prophètes, même si quelqu’un ressuscite d’entre les morts, ils ne seront pas persuadés.” »
fr.B: Abraham lui a dit : “S’ils ne veulent pas écouter Moïse et les prophètes, même quelqu’un qui se relèverait d’entre les morts ne les persuadera pas.” »
fr.R: Abraham lui a répondu : “Si tes frères ne veulent pas écouter Moïse et les prophètes, ils ne seront pas convaincus non plus, même si quelqu’un revient à la vie après être mort.” »

sw.L: Lakini akamwambia, 'Kama hawawasikilizi Musa na manabii, hawatasadiki hata ikiwa mtu atafufuka kutoka kwa wafu.'"
sw.B: Ibrahimu alimwambia, 'Ikiwa hawataki kuwasikiliza Musa na manabii, hata mtu akifufuka kutoka kwa wafu hatawasadikisha.'"
sw.R: Ibrahimu alimwambia, 'Ikiwa ndugu zako hawawasikilizi Musa na manabii, hawataamini hata mtu akirudi kuwa hai kutoka kwa wafu.'"

decisions.choice: if someone rises from the dead: pointing ahead to Jesus' own resurrection
decisions.reason: The words fit what Luke goes on to tell: Jesus rose from the dead, and even then many were not persuaded. The risen Jesus explains himself from Moses and all the prophets (24:25-27, 44-46).

decisions.choice: will be persuaded: will be convinced and change their ways
decisions.reason: The verb means to be won over. A sign from the dead will not change a heart that will not hear God's word.

decisions.choice: rises: is raised to life
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for rising from the dead (18:33; 24:7, 46). It is stronger than "goes to them" in 16:30.

decisions.choice: Abraham
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the speaker.

decisions.choice: Abraham's words and Jesus' speech close here
decisions.reason: The parable ends with the chapter.
